items.title: How AI Could Bring Halo and Other Classic Games Back to Life
items.summary: AI tooling and agentic workflows are collapsing the barrier between game ideas and playable prototypes, drastically shortening development cycles, and enabling niche genres and remix-driven mods that were previously economically unviable.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
AI tooling and agentic workflows are collapsing the barrier between game ideas and playable prototypes, drastically shortening development cycles, and enabling niche genres and remix-driven mods that were previously economically unviable.

## AI Tools and Technical Unlock
* **Direct Tool Operation:** **Jonathan Lai** notes a major technology unlock occurred when models like **Astra** gained the ability to directly operate popular game development software (like **Blender**, **Unreal Engine**, and **Unity**) rather than merely giving text instructions.
* **Autonomous QA and Coding:** **Anish Acharya** highlights how models like **Opus 47/48** demonstrated native 3JS (in-browser 3D) manipulation and layout capabilities, while **Astra** can autonomously take screen caps and QA its own output to fix bugs.
* **Browser 3D Acceleration:** **Jonathan Lai** points to modern web GPU and 3JS capabilities enabling classic titles like **Halo** (the 2001 original Xbox game) and other retro titles to be decompiled, recompiled, and played directly in web browsers.

## Shorter Development Cycles and Creative Risk
* **The AAA Bottleneck:** **Jonathan Lai** points out that blockbuster games like **Grand Theft Auto 6** have massive 12-13 year development cycles (in production since 2013-2014), which creates a suffocating impact on industry innovation.
* **Lowering Budgets and Timelines:** **Jonathan Lai** explains that cutting development timelines from 5-10 years down to 2-5 years, and lowering costs from hundreds of millions to tens of millions of dollars, will allow studios to greenlight new IPs and take creative risks rather than relying on endless sequels like the 20th installment of **Call of Duty**.
* **Esoteric Genres:** **Jonathan Lai** notes that Epic CEO **Tim Sweeney** highlighted how faster prototyping allows developers to economically build niche and esoteric genres that previously would not have been viable.

## Democratization and Creation as Play
* **Lowering Skill Barriers:** **Jonathan Lai** discusses how AI bridges the multidisciplinary gaps of coding, art, game design, and music, allowing hobbyists and tinkerers to build game prototypes without professional training.
* **Zen Gardening:** **Anish Acharya** argues that in the AI era, creation often acts as consumption—where the act of building a game and watching assets come to life provides a tranquil, playful "zen gardening" experience, even if a game is only played by its creator.
* **Real-World Examples:** 
  * **Anish Acharya** built a 1990s Habbo Hotel-themed record shop and expanded it into Queen Street in Toronto using **Opus 55**, featuring interactive music tracks and storefronts where his son built a functional pet adoption center.
  * **Jonathan Lai** shares that his eight-year-old son used **ChatGPT** to deconstruct game mechanics and build a fully functioning **Minecraft mod** of *Ghost of Tsushima*.

## Modding, Remixing, and Decompilation
* **Historical Precedent:** **Jonathan Lai** notes that multi-billion-dollar franchises originated as mods, such as **Counter-Strike** (a *Half-Life* mod), **League of Legends** (inspired by *Defense of the Ancients/Dota*, a *Warcraft 3* mod), and **PUBG/Fortnite** (inspired by *Arma* battle royale mods).
* **Decompilation and Remasters:** **Anish Acharya** highlights community efforts to decompile classic games like *Knights of the Old Republic*, while **Jonathan Lai** notes **Xbox** is leaning into AI-assisted porting and preservation following community web-GPU recreations of classic titles.
* **Cross-Asset Merging:** **Anish Acharya** points to creator **Blendy (@BL_NDI)** on X, who takes assets from two existing games and combines them into entirely new, functional games.

## Emerging Ecosystems, Distribution, and Future Genres
* **Never-Ending Games:** **Jonathan Lai** outlines the "holy grail" concept of an MMO or world model that infinitely adapts quest lines and mechanics to player choices on the fly (reminiscent of the "mind game" from *Ender's Game*).
* **New Platform Models:** **Anish Acharya** highlights **Spawn** (built by Jacob and team), a shared community and game generation platform featuring an embodied agent named **Savvy** that acts as an in-game co-op developer and portal creator.
* **Simulation and RTS Renaissance:** Both speakers predict a resurgence in simulation games (like job/train simulators) and Real-Time Strategy (RTS) games, alongside AI-native dating sims and agent-orchestration interfaces styled after games like *Age of Empires*.

## Notable Quotes
> "It's like Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally coming out next month and like that game has been in production since like 2013 2014. It's like a 12 13 year development cycle... by any other software development standard, right? Like taking 10 plus years to make... [it] is kind of insane."
> — **Jonathan Lai**

> "AI model is not going to replace human taste and creative judgment. I think that is still really really critical... The last 20% of the game is 80% of the work. And that's where all the magic comes together to make something fun."
> — **Jonathan Lai**

> "Sometimes creation is consumption. The vast majority of games are ever going to be played by one person that is the creator in the future. And that's okay actually... there's a sort of zen gardening aspect to game creation which will become increasingly popular."
> — **Anish Acharya**

items.title: Lisa Su on why investing ahead of the AI curve is the right thing to do
items.summary: AMD Chair and CEO Dr. Lisa Su discussed the company's rapid acceleration driven by surging AI demand—highlighting that demand currently exceeds supply and that market worries over AI spending are short-sighted given that compute equates to intelligence.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
AMD Chair and CEO Dr. Lisa Su discussed the company's rapid acceleration driven by surging AI demand—highlighting that demand currently exceeds supply and that market worries over AI spending are short-sighted given that compute equates to intelligence. The discussion was hosted by Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi, who presented Dr. Su with Yahoo Finance's CEO of the Year award.

## 1. AMD's Transformation and Strategic Milestones
* **Long-Term Strategic Bets:** **Decade-Long Evolution:** Dr. Su noted that technology decisions require three to five years to come to fruition, with AMD making systematic, multi-year bets on high-performance computing.
  * **Product Generations:** The company is now advancing its sixth generation of EPYC Italian-city-named CPU products.
* **Scale and Visibility:** **Rising Profile:** AMD has transitioned from being considered one of tech's "best kept secrets" between 2015 and 2018 into a prominent industry leader with frequent White House engagements.
  * **Leadership Approach:** Dr. Su emphasized that her own role has evolved into constant learning alongside industry partners during an unprecedented technology cycle.

## 2. Market Dynamics and the Rise of AI Agents
* **The AI Inflection Point:** **Compute as Intelligence:** Dr. Su asserted that computing is the foundation of AI and that "compute equates to intelligence," making investments ahead of the curve essential for long-term progress.
  * **Ecosystem Collaboration:** Rejecting the idea of a single winning semiconductor model, Su stressed that success relies on deep partnerships across the ecosystem between chipmakers, frontier model labs, and hyperscalers.
* **The Impact of Personal Agents:** **Rapid Adoption:** The conversation highlighted the emergence of personal agents (such as Muse, which reached 10 million activations in 45 days) as a massive new demand driver.
  * **Shift in Planning:** Traditional annual static enterprise operating plans are being replaced by dynamic adoption curves, fueling continuous quarterly increases in demand for both CPUs and GPUs.

## 3. Financial Outlook and Supply-Demand Realities
* **Guidance and Projections:** **Revenue and Data Center Scale:** AMD's Q3 into Q4 guidance targets over $50 billion in revenue for the year, with the data center business projected to grow over 100% (more than doubling) compared to the prior year.
  * **Sequential Acceleration:** Data center revenue is guided to grow 50% sequentially from Q3 to Q4.
* **Supply Constraints:** **Exceeding Capacity:** Dr. Su stated that demand currently outpaces what AMD can supply, allowing the company to quickly backfill any isolated project delays by reallocating capacity to customers who need more.
  * **Customer Partnerships:** AMD maintains deep, ongoing relationships with top hyperscalers and model developers—including OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic, Microsoft, Oracle, Amazon, and Google—all of which are continuously asking for more computing capacity.

## 4. Public Perception and Data Center Infrastructure
* **Community Engagement:** **Proactive Storytelling:** Addressing public concerns over data center expansion, Dr. Su emphasized that the tech industry must be front-footed and proactive at the local level.
  * **Local Benefits:** She stressed the importance of communicating how data centers contribute to energy infrastructure, local economic growth, job creation, and ensuring that communities directly share in the benefits of American technological leadership.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Lisa Su:** AMD will grow the overall company by more than 80% in the year 2027.
* **Lisa Su:** AMD's data center business will more than double (grow over 100%) in the current year.
* **Lisa Su:** Demand for computing power will continue to outpace supply across multiple quarters.

## Notable Quotes
> "The best way to say it is, you know, the reason I joined AMD was I wanted to be part of a company that really could be at the bleeding edge of technology... And so if I fast forward, you know, 10 years later, I think what I can say, you know, firmly today is, you know, we are driving the bleeding edge of technology."
> — Dr. Lisa Su

> "I believe very, you know, deeply that computing in many ways equates to intelligence. So the more compute you have, the more intelligent you are, the more intelligent your company is... If you believe that foundation, then investing ahead of the curve is the right thing to do."
> — Dr. Lisa Su

> "Anyone who tells you they know all the answers is just wrong because frankly, you know, every month there's new developments. Like we're surprised. Like you know, look at what's happened over the last 30 to 45 days. Look how much personal agents have come into the conversation."
> — Dr. Lisa Su

items.title: Palantir CEO warns the AI boom could make the rich 20x richer
items.summary: Palantir CEO Alex Karp and former Senator Jon Tester discuss the 2024 midterm election results, warning that unchecked AI growth risks drastically widening income inequality and fueling political backlash unless tech leaders and politicians prioritize economic justice.
items.content_text:
- **TL;DR:** Palantir CEO Alex Karp and former Senator Jon Tester discuss the 2024 midterm election results, warning that unchecked AI growth risks drastically widening income inequality and fueling political backlash unless tech leaders and politicians prioritize economic justice. The conversation also covers Palantir's government contracts, the demand for government competence, and immigration oversight.

## Election Results and Economic Inequality
- **Referendum on Economic Justice:** Alex Karp argues that recent midterm election results reflect deep-seated voter anxiety over income inequality and economic fairness.
- **The AI Wealth Gap:** Karp warns that the AI revolution threatens to make top tech executives "20 to 50 times wealthier" while average workers see only minor gains (3% to 5% wage growth before inflation).
- **Flaws in Free-Market Dogma:** Karp criticizes the right-wing orthodoxy that capitalism automatically solves all societal problems, arguing that wealth concentration without shared prosperity is politically unsustainable.
- **The Appeal of the Democratic Socialists (DSA):** Jon Tester notes that the rise of the DSA and income disparity are symptoms of an economy that is "way, way, way too wide" in its wealth gap.
- **Desire for Checks and Balances:** Tester states that voters sent a message demanding government oversight, accountability, and a return to government working for working families, family farms, and small businesses.

## Palantir's Business and "Sovereign AI"
- **Commercial Growth:** Karp highlights that Palantir's commercial business is the dominant driver of its valuation, noting that **US commercial revenue is growing at nearly 150%**.
- **Market Valuation:** Karp attributes Palantir's **$400 billion to $500 billion market cap** heavily to its success in US commercial markets and sovereign AI leadership.
- **Sovereign AI Movement:** Palantir defines its commercial success as pioneering "sovereign AI," pushing businesses to control their own means of production to generate shared value for shareholders and workers rather than outsourcing it.
- **Defending the Fourth Amendment:** Karp explicitly rejects the notion that Palantir's mission compromises civil liberties, calling the company one of the "most important defenders of the Fourth Amendment right in this country."

## Government Efficiency, Oversight, and Immigration
- **Restoring Trust in Government:** Jon Tester, joining Palantir in an advisory role, emphasizes that software-driven efficiency can restore faith in government, optimize taxpayer dollars, and aid warfighters and agricultural workers.
- **Congressional Oversight:** Tester advises that if Palantir faces scrutiny from a Democratic-led Congress, the company should simply be transparent, forthright, and respectful, treating congressional oversight as a healthy check and balance.
- **Immigration Policy Missteps:** Karp praises President Trump for publicly acknowledging that ICE enforcement went "too far," stating that he previously advised leaders in private that immigration enforcement must be handled competently, humanely, and fairly to retain public support.
- **Political Neutrality:** Karp maintains that Palantir is a product-driven organization focused on high competence rather than a political entity, noting that his political donations are balanced across both Democrats and Republicans.

## Industry Titans and the 2028 Political Landscape
- **Support for Jensen Huang:** Karp expresses strong support for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, describing him as an irreplaceable titan of the AI industry who is handling current transparency challenges with integrity.
- **Open 2028 Democratic Field:** Jon Tester predicts the 2028 Democratic primary will be wide open—comparing it dynamically to the 2008 cycle—and will be won by an outsider who "catches fire" with a compelling forward-looking plan.
- **Prerequisite for Support:** Karp states he will financially support and rally his tens of millions of supporters behind whichever political leader—Democrat or otherwise—prioritizes economic justice, competence, and fairness over ideological extremism.

## Notable Quotes
> "You have a revolution that is making people like me potentially 20 times richer. Go explain to the American people why that's justified. You can't." — Alex Karp

> "The folks who can't claim victory are the folks that didn't stand up and hold this president of this administration accountable. It's the folks that didn't stand up and say, 'Hey, we're going to do oversight hearings.'" — Jon Tester

> "If you do not explain to the American people why it is a small group of people... that are becoming 20, 40, 50 times wealthier and you're maximally going to become 5% wealthier before you deduct inflation, see how they react." — Alex Karp

> "Do your homework. Make sure you got your facts in line. Ask tough questions. Demand answers." — Jon Tester

items.title: Powering AI-Driven Drug Discovery with President of Isomorphic Labs Max Jaderberg
items.summary: Isomorphic Labs is shifting drug discovery from empirical trial-and-error to computer-aided precision engineering by using predictive AI models to achieve experimental accuracy.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Isomorphic Labs is shifting drug discovery from empirical trial-and-error to computer-aided precision engineering by using predictive AI models to achieve experimental accuracy. Founded in 2021 as an Alphabet-backed spin-out inspired by AlphaFold, the company builds disease-, target-, and modality-agnostic drug design engines to tackle diseases like cancer and immunology.

## AI & The Paradigm Shift in Drug Discovery
* **The Empirical Bottleneck:** **Max Jaderberg** notes that the pharma industry has historically relied on trial-and-error, guessing molecules without understanding their mechanisms (e.g., aspirin and paracetamol).
  * Drug development has grown increasingly difficult, expensive (~$1.5B per drug), and slow (up to 15 years), while new drug approvals remain flat despite an explosion of scientific knowledge and modalities.
  * The human cell is a high-dimensional chaotic system, and molecule design (small molecules, antibodies, peptides) is combinatorially large, limiting the complexity of solutions reachable via manual screening.
* **The Generalizability of AI:** **Max Jaderberg** explains that the success of AlphaFold served as the first proof of concept that deep learning models could generalize in meaningful biological spaces.
  * Unlike traditional pharma projects treated as bespoke frontier science projects with little transferable learning, Isomorphic's AI platform captures compounding learnings across medicines to achieve economies of scale in R&D.

## Isomorphic Labs: Approach, Models, & Data Strategy
* **Cross-Disciplinary Teams:** **Max Jaderberg** highlights that Isomorphic hires core AI/deep learning researchers (who may lack life sciences backgrounds) and pairs them with biology and chemistry domain experts in roughly a 1-in-5 ratio within problem pods.
* **In-Silico Simulation vs. Real World:** **Max Jaderberg** states the North Star is bringing drug discovery entirely onto computers to bypass the time and cost bottleneck of synthesizing real atoms.
  * **Experimental Accuracy:** Isomorphic tracks a benchmark target on all leaderboards aiming for "experimental accuracy," meaning models become so predictive that researchers do not need to run real-world assays for every iteration.
  * Real-world laboratories, CROs, and automated robotic systems are used to generate proprietary data and validate hypotheses rather than drive slow trial-and-error iteration loops.
* **Therapeutic Focus & Disease Agnosticism:** **Max Jaderberg** shares that Isomorphic's internal pipeline focuses on oncology, immunology, and inflammation—targeting "root node" problems like RAS mutations (e.g., Kraz inhibitors).
  * The underlying AI drug design engine is entirely agnostic of disease area, target class, and modality.

## Clinical Trials, Toxicity, & Future Therapeutics
* **Overcoming Clinical Failure:** **Max Jaderberg** points out that drugs primarily fail in clinical trials due to uncounted toxicities and off-target effects that only surface when introduced to real human patients.
  * Animal models (like rats) are only about 30% predictive of human clinical toxicity. Isomorphic aims to replace animal proxies with in vitro endpoints, predictive AI models, and emerging technologies like organoids and organs-on-a-chip.
* **Enabling Multi-Drug Cocktails:** **Max Jaderberg** argues that current medicine relies on single targets because poor molecule engineering creates harmful drug-drug interactions and liver toxicities when combined. Precise molecular engineering could unlock safe, complex multi-drug cocktails capable of suppressing multi-mutational diseases like cancer and HIV simultaneously.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Max Jaderberg** states he would be really disappointed if, in 5 years, the predictive understanding of disease biology and molecule design has not step-changed massively to shorten multi-year drug development timelines.

## Notable Quotes
> "The large part of the industry makes medicines is this very empirically driven process... where things really fail is in the clinic because we never could see the problems until we get to the point where we put these drugs in patients."
> — **Max Jaderberg**

> "We think about going after literally just the best people in core AI and deep learning who maybe don't even have a background in life sciences or biology or chemistry, but really want to see their work on deep learning translate into amazing impact for humanity."
> — **Max Jaderberg**

> "Internally we have a dotted line on all of our leaderboards that is experimental accuracy... At that point, you don't need to go into the real world. You can do so much more design and iteration on a computer."
> — **Max Jaderberg**

items.title: Why are electric vehicles still the ‘car of the future’?
items.summary: While electric vehicles (EVs) are cleaner and cheaper to run, the global transition is progressing unevenly due to upfront vehicle costs, charging infrastructure gaps, and regional policy divergences.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR:** While electric vehicles (EVs) are cleaner and cheaper to run, the global transition is progressing unevenly due to upfront vehicle costs, charging infrastructure gaps, and regional policy divergences. 

## The Current State of EV Adoption & Fleet Turnover
* **Global Sales vs. Existing Fleet:** 
  * In 2025, fully electric cars and plug-in hybrids together accounted for 25% (1 out of 4) of new car sales worldwide.
  * Only about 5% of cars currently on the road are electric or plug-in hybrids, out of an existing global installed base of 1.3 to 1.4 billion cars (**Laia Barbarà**).
* **Regional Divergences:**
  * **China:** Operating as the global frontrunner/mecca of EVs, almost the entire new car fleet sold is electric, driven by strong policy alignment, subsidies, and aggressive export scaling (**Laia Barbarà**, **Elaine Buckberg**, **Paul Farrell**).
  * **Europe:** EV sales grew around 30% year-over-year, but the region faces policy friction trying to balance affordability, locally made vehicles, and job retention (**Laia Barbarà**).
  * **North America:** Adoption has experienced slower growth and fits-and-starts compared to Europe, though hybrid vehicle adoption continues to grow alongside shifting federal priorities (**Paul Farrell**).

## Consumer Psychology & Lifestyle Barriers
* **Upfront Cost vs. Long-Term Savings:** While EVs are cheaper to run (especially with home charging), high upfront purchase prices remain a primary hurdle for budget-constrained consumers (**Laia Barbarà**, **Paul Farrell**).
* **Range Anxiety & The "Extreme Use Case":** 
  * Only 1% to 2% of Americans drive a trip longer than 100 miles each way annually, yet consumers buy cars based on extreme use cases like annual family road trips (**Elaine Buckberg**).
  * Studies (such as research by Christian Kaps and Mike Toffel at Harvard Business School) show that actual EV owners utilize similar driving and charging patterns to internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicle owners once they have a vehicle with at least 250 miles of range (**Elaine Buckberg**).
* **Urban & Multi-Family Housing Challenges:** Apartment dwellers and city residents lacking home garages or dedicated parking rely heavily on accessible public curbside or supermarket charging (**Laia Barbarà**, **Elaine Buckberg**, **Paul Farrell**).

## Infrastructure & Energy System Integration
* **Grid Reliability and Investment:** 
  * The massive scale of electrification requires significant, costly investments in power grids, transmission operators, and charging networks (such as Iberdrola and BP Pulse's joint venture in Spain and Portugal) (**Agustin Delgado**).
  * Power systems require proper technical mechanisms and specialized workforces to maintain high reliability, underscored by wake-up calls like the past Iberian blackout (**Agustin Delgado**).
* **Charging Infrastructure Deployment:** 
  * Solutions range from home time-of-use tariffs (costing under €2 per 100 kilometers) to highway safety charging networks and fast-charging hubs at supermarkets (**Agustin Delgado**, **Elaine Buckberg**).
  * Government policies like California and Massachusetts' "right-to-charge" rules help condo and apartment owners install home chargers (**Elaine Buckberg**).

## Industry Strategy & Supply Chain Transformation
* **Resilient Portfolios:** Tier-1 suppliers like BorgWarner have spent the last decade building flexible, resilient portfolios spanning combustion, hybrids, and full battery-electric vehicles to adapt to varying regional paces (**Paul Farrell**).
* **Economies of Scale:** As EV production scales from niche to mainstream across a 90-million-unit annual passenger car market, manufacturing efficiencies, battery cost reductions, and technological maturity are driving down costs (**Paul Farrell**).
* **Global Competition:** The transition is heavily influenced by international competition between China, the U.S., and Europe, forcing incumbent industries to embrace new technologies rather than protect old ones (**Agustin Delgado**, **Paul Farrell**).

## Notable Quotes
> "The bottom line is we have to make the cleaner choice the easier choice in everyday life, and that's both for companies and individuals."
> — **Laia Barbarà**

> "It is a non-regret decision. It is no brain that this technology will be the most used technology, and not in 100 years, but in a period shorter than we think."
> — **Agustin Delgado**

> "One of the things I learned as chief economist of General Motors is that people buy vehicles for their extreme use case."
> — **Elaine Buckberg**

> "We have to think less in terms of the ability to get to the perfect forecast. And it's a lot more about saying, all right, I can't predict that, how do I make sure I'm positioned so that I can adjust or we can adjust based on how the market evolves."
> — **Paul Farrell**

items.title: AlphaGenome 2: Teaching AI to read the entire human genome
items.summary: Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome and AlphaGenome 2 are AI models designed to read the 98% non-coding human genome at single-cell resolution, helping researchers decode how genetic variants drive complex diseases and rare conditions.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome and AlphaGenome 2 are AI models designed to read the 98% non-coding human genome at single-cell resolution, helping researchers decode how genetic variants drive complex diseases and rare conditions.

## The Human Genome and the Genotype-Phenotype Gap
* **Genotype vs. Phenotype:** **Genotype** refers to the 3 billion letters of human DNA (A, C, G, T), while **phenotype** is defined at the cellular level—specifically how genes change their expression across different cell types.
* **The Non-Coding Mystery:** **The 2% vs. 98% divide:** Only 2% of the genome encodes proteins (the "LEGO building blocks"), while the remaining 98% regulates when and where those proteins are produced across various cell types.
* **Complex vs. Mendelian Diseases:** 
  * **Mendelian diseases** involve a variant directly causing a disease (e.g., BRCA1 and certain cancers, though even these are complex).
  * **Complex diseases** involve a risk profile determined by a combination of genetic background and environmental factors.

## Evolution of DeepMind's Genomic Models
* **AlphaFold & AlphaMissense:** **Protein-level focus:** After AlphaFold 2 mapped protein structures, DeepMind developed **AlphaMissense** to fine-tune protein structure predictions into pathogenicity scores for coding mutations.
* **AlphaGenome (2025):** **Whole-tissue context:** Expanded sequence input from 200,000 to 1 million base pairs and increased resolution from 128 base pairs down to a single base pair to predict non-coding DNA function across whole tissues.
* **AlphaGenome Atlas:** **Pre-computed variant impacts:** Contains 9 billion pre-computed letter changes across the human genome, condensing 10,000 output numbers plus evolutionary conservation into a single **AVVAI score** (AlphaGenome Variant Impact Score) ranging from 0 to ~80 to rank mutations.
* **AlphaGenome 2:** **Single-cell resolution:** Upgraded to predict cell-type-specific variant effects (such as in macrophages or blood cells) and allows laboratories to plug in their own custom data without retraining the model.

## Real-World Applications and Case Studies
* **Rare Disease Prioritization:** **Pediatric epilepsy case:** Researchers at the Broad Institute used the AVVAI score to narrow down a list of suspect variants in a 6-week-old baby diagnosed with rare epilepsy, successfully identifying a splicing variant 4 to 5 years later and validating it experimentally via a cell-line assay.
* **GWAS Bottlenecks:** **Unpacking linkage disequilibrium:** Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) often identify correlated chunks of inherited DNA rather than true causal variants; AlphaGenome helps prioritize causal variants, target genes, and relevant cell types.
* **Tool Limitations:** **High-precision, low-recall:** The models act as research tools rather than clinical diagnostics, functioning effectively to flag high-impact variants while occasionally missing edge cases due to the "bowl of spaghetti" physical compaction of DNA.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **AGI vs. Virtual Cell:** "I think we're going to have AGI before we have a virtual cell. That's my prediction. I think you're probably right. Intelligence is less hard than biology, it seems." — Adam Gayoso

## Notable Quotes
> "We bought the book, but it's quite hard to read. But now with AI, that book is gradually becoming more legible."
> — Professor Hannah Fry (quoting geneticist Eric Lander)

> "Life has had four billion years weaving everything into this unimaginable complexity. And by contrast, our genome [AI models] is only 18 months old."
> — Professor Hannah Fry

items.title: Donald Trump; France on Fire | 60 Minutes Full Broadcast
items.summary: President Donald Trump reflects on a brutal midterm election defeat, foreign policy, and his controversial business ties in a post-election interview, while across the Atlantic, severe economic protests in France threaten to catapult right-wing populist Marine Le Pen to the presidency.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
President Donald Trump reflects on a brutal midterm election defeat, foreign policy, and his controversial business ties in a post-election interview, while across the Atlantic, severe economic protests in France threaten to catapult right-wing populist Marine Le Pen to the presidency.

## Trump's Post-Midterm Reflection and Policy Stance
* **Midterm Repudiation:** **Republican Election Losses:** President Trump acknowledged his party's historic defeat in the midterms—losing the House, Senate, and red-state offices in Texas, Kansas, and South Carolina—attributing the backlash to voter dislike of high gasoline prices, the war in Iran, and unfavorable views of Israel.
* **Immigration & Deportation Reevaluation:** **Too Tough Policy:** Trump admitted his mass deportation policy "might be too tough" and acknowledged that removing long-term, working immigrants from hotels and landscaping businesses hurt him politically.
* **Bipartisan Outreach:** **Working with Democrats:** Despite past insults (such as calling a new Texas Democratic senator "Clapperico"), Trump expressed openness to working with Democrats on immigration reform and avoiding future impeachments.
* **White House Staff Shakeup:** **Leadership Changes:** Just an hour after the 60 Minutes interview, Chief of Staff Susie Wiles was replaced by deputy chief Steven Miller, the architect of the mass deportation policy.

## Foreign Policy: Iran, Ukraine, and Defense
* **The Iran War and Nuclear Program:** **Decapitation Strikes:** Trump defended his decision to authorize decapitation strikes on Iran's nuclear facilities using B-2 bombers, claiming the war is essentially over and that Iran's nuclear material is "buried under thousands of tons of rock."
* **Cost Recovery:** **Nation Reimbursement:** Trump asserted that protected allies, including Israel, will eventually pay back the U.S. for all costs incurred during the Iran war.
* **Defense Leadership:** **Support for Pete Hegseth:** Trump reaffirmed his full confidence in Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, crediting him with winning the conflict in Venezuela in less than an hour.
* **Russia-Ukraine War:** **Imminent Peace Deal:** Trump claimed he inherited the conflict due to hatred between Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelenskyy, expressed confidence that the war will end soon because of his intervention, and noted he recently lifted diesel sanctions on Russia to supply global energy needs.

## Wealth, Crypto, and Potential Corruption Allegations
* **Net Worth Speculation:** **Forbes Estimates:** Trump denied that his net worth surged by $3 billion since returning to office, stating he devotes almost no time to his finances and highlighting that he is the only president who does not take a salary.
* **Crypto and Foreign Ties:** **World Liberty Financial:** When questioned about potential conflicts of interest regarding his son managing the crypto firm World Liberty Financial—which features investments from United Arab Emirates-connected entities—Trump dismissed the concerns, comparing it to the real estate business of his sons and arguing that every president faces unavoidable conflicts.

## Silicon Valley, AI Superintelligence, and UFOs
* **The AI Race with China:** **Super Intelligence (SI):** Trump described himself as an "AI bull," explaining that the U.S. is locked in a high-stakes race with China, where President Xi Jinping is "all in" on super intelligence.
* **Risk Management:** **Dismissing Doom:** Trump rejected Silicon Valley warnings that AI carries a 10% chance of killing humanity, arguing that the risks are exaggerated and manageable, and warning that falling behind China is not an option.
* **UFO Sightings:** **Military Pilot Accounts:** Trump noted that while he is "not too much of a believer," he has held private meetings with top F-22 Air Force pilots who reported encountering round, non-aerodynamic objects traveling at three times their speed.

## Mortality and Unforgiving Views on Political Rivals
* **Views on the Afterlife:** **Heaven and Hell:** As a religious person, Trump stated he hopes to go to heaven and avoid hell, but refused to express forgiveness for his political enemies.
* **Refusing Reconciliation:** **Hatred of Rivals:** When asked if he could forgive figures like James Comey or Nancy Pelosi to enter paradise, Trump bluntly replied: "I probably cannot do that, no, because I do hate some of my enemies, and I always will."

## France on Fire: Economic Unrest and the Rise of Marine Le Pen
* **National Upheaval:** **Widespread Chaos:** Weeks of protests in France—sparked originally by high school student demonstrations over dilapidated schools and a lack of toilet paper—have ballooned into nationwide riots over economic inequality, capitalism, and President Emmanuel Macron's leadership.
* **Economic Toll:** **Billion-Dollar Damages:** The unrest has damaged 2,500 businesses, injured over 1,500 police officers, and caused more than $1 billion in property damage, including the burning of the historic Limoges town hall and the ransacking of immigrant-owned bakeries like Jemi Maschila's.
* **Marine Le Pen's Populist Rise:** **Presidential Frontrunner:** Marine Le Pen, long-time leader of the National Rally Party, has seen her popularity surge amidst the chaos, positioning her as the favorite to win next April's presidential election.
* **Immigration and Remigration:** **Stricter Borders:** Le Pen blamed immigration for destabilizing French society, rejected claims of racism or discrimination in France, and proposed a "remigration" policy to force out immigrants who express hatred for French culture and laws.

## Notable Quotes
> *"I think it might be too tough, yeah. And I think ultimately I think ultimately that hurt me."* — **President Donald Trump**, on his mass deportation policy.

> *"I probably cannot do that, no, because I do hate some of my enemies, and I always will."* — **President Donald Trump**, when asked if he could forgive political rivals like James Comey and Nancy Pelosi to enter heaven.

> *"The extreme left creates chaos. They generate violence against people, against the police, against public property. It's the same phenomenon all over."* — **Marine Le Pen**, on the forces driving the French protests.

> *"If someone comes and says I hate you, I despise your culture, I don't want to respect your laws, well, we say to him, listen, sir, the door is wide open. And we might even, for that matter, force you to leave."* — **Marine Le Pen**, detailing her immigration stance.

items.title: GLP-1s Are a Bigger Business Than AI
items.summary: Zach Reitano, co-founder and CEO of Ro, argues that the central flaw in the American healthcare system is that the patient is not the customer.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Zach Reitano, co-founder and CEO of Ro, argues that the central flaw in the American healthcare system is that the patient is not the customer. Where patients pay directly—such as with LASIC or when GLP-1 drug prices dropped from $1,300 to $149 by cutting out PBMs—costs fall, quality improves, and care is transformed.

## Healthcare System Structure & Economic Realities
* **Systemic Flaw:** The core dysfunction of U.S. healthcare is that the patient is not the customer; whoever controls the flow of money at the point of purchase dictates the system.
* **Spending Breakdown & GDP Share:** 
  * Healthcare spending sits at 18% of U.S. GDP.
  * ~30-35% of U.S. healthcare dollars go to hospital systems, 20-25% to doctor's offices, and 9-10% to drugs and pharmaceuticals.
  * The U.S. spends ~50% of its healthcare costs on 5% of people.
* **Acute vs. Chronic Care:** The U.S. healthcare system excels at acute care (cancer survival rates, heart attacks, strokes are higher on average than OECD countries), but struggles with the "slow clock" of rising chronic disease.
* **Cash-Pay Precedents:** Where cash-pay models operate directly, costs drop and quality rises (e.g., LASIC eye surgery, breast augmentation, and direct-to-consumer GLP-1s).
* **The PBM Monopoly:** Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) add administrative bloat and friction. When GLP-1s went direct-to-consumer, list-to-net pricing intermediaries were eliminated, dropping prices from $1,300 to $149 while drugmakers actually captured more gross profit via massive volume.

## Ro’s Business & Product Lineup
* **Growth Metrics:** Ro scaled from a $250 million run rate to over a $3 billion run rate with fewer people than in 2021 (dropping from 600+ to 400+ employees while 10xing the business).
* **Four Core Categories:** 
  * Cardio-metabolic health (fastest-growing, anchored by GLP-1s).
  * Sexual health.
  * Dermatology.
  * Fertility.
* **Infrastructure & Integration:** Ro built an EMR from scratch, a CLIA-certificate CAP-accredited lab, pharmacies, provider networks, and custom pharmacy software in a condition-agnostic, vertically integrated platform.
* **Insurance & Direct Access:** Ro has helped over 1% of the U.S. population check their insurance for free using AI, and offers multi-month subscriptions saving patients $600 to $1,800 annually.

## The GLP-1 Revolution & Human Biology
* **Upstream Impact:** GLP-1s treat the root causes of major chronic killers—approved for diabetes, obesity, overweight, heart disease, sleep apnea, liver disease, and kidney disease, with ongoing studies for addiction, nerve degeneration, pain management, and cancer prevention.
* **Rewiring Incentives:** The majority of GLP-1 growth is direct-to-consumer cash pay, bypassing traditional employer-sponsored constraints and proving that price transparency and direct access work.
* **Societal Parallels:** Just as conquering infant mortality, maternal mortality, and infectious disease sparked the Industrial Revolution, tackling chronic diseases upstream will fundamentally reshape human society.

## The 2022 Company Refounding & Operational Playbook
* **The Zombie Phase (December 2021):** Despite raising $500 million at a $5 billion valuation in January 2021, Ro grew only 9% that year, burning cash with an $800M preference stack and suffering from a bloated, unfocused culture ("macaroon soft").
* **The Reset (Summer 2022):** 
  * Replaced ~7 VPs between January and May 2022; cut 20% of the organization in May-June.
  * Co-founder Rob passed the baton; all brands were consolidated under the single "Ro" name.
  * Implemented a strict "Strong Attract, Strong Repel" culture with explicitly defined operational principles and a zero-ambiguity "work hard" ethos. An additional 6-7% opted out.
* **Execution & Focus:**
  * **Sequential vs. Parallel Building:** Leaned into sequential development rather than parallel to avoid context-switching and maximize compounding gains.
  * **Daily Alignment:** Maintained a daily 8:50 AM leadership steering meeting for two straight years to enforce velocity and accountability.
  * **Killing Long-Term Roadmaps:** Replaced multi-year roadmaps with short-term precision and long-term vision, treating detailed long-term plans as "false precision."

## Marketing, Stigma, and Consumer Psychology
* **Permission Structures:** Ro uses high-profile brand ambassadors (Serena Williams, Charles Barkley, Megan Fox, Chrissy Mets) to dismantle stigma and create cultural permission structures for patients seeking care for weight loss, sexual health, and preventative screenings.
* **Stigma as a Signpost:** Societal tension and discomfort around preventative medications (like GLP-1s or cholesterol treatments) highlight irrational double standards compared to socially accepted health-negative behaviors like alcohol consumption.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **GLP-1 Adoption:** Zach Reitano predicts that **50% plus of people** will be on some form of a GLP-1 10 years from now. — Zach Reitano

## Notable Quotes
> "If I had to say like what is the problem with our healthcare system, it is that the patient is not the customer. Whoever controls the flow of money at the point of purchase. That's the customer."
> — Zach Reitano

> "We as a society, especially when it comes to health, must prioritize outcomes over inputs. The new thing must prove its worth... And I do believe that the people impeding driverless cars where they are proven to be safe should have a body count attached to their name truly."
> — Zach Reitano

> "No one gives a shit about the packaging when you are winning as a company."
> — Zach Reitano

items.title: Inside Theranos with ex-Employee Tyler Shultz
items.summary: Tyler Shultz details his transition from an enthralled Theranos employee and mentee of Elizabeth Holmes to a primary whistleblower who exposed systemic fraudulent medical testing, battling aggressive legal intimidation by the company before finding personal and professional vindication.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Tyler Shultz details his transition from an enthralled Theranos employee and mentee of Elizabeth Holmes to a primary whistleblower who exposed systemic fraudulent medical testing, battling aggressive legal intimidation by the company before finding personal and professional vindication.

## Background & Early Experience
* **Initial Impression:** 
    * Recruited out of Stanford after meeting Elizabeth Holmes at his grandfather George Shultz's house; initially viewed her as "the next Steve Jobs."
    * Sold on the transformative vision of running any central laboratory test on a single drop of blood anywhere in the world.
* **Early Red Flags:**
    * Completed a summer internship working on antibody engineering far removed from the core device, noticing extreme workplace siloing, locked doors, and no co-workers who had actually seen the product.
    * A parting warning from a colleague: *"You shouldn't come back here. You should go somewhere else and learn how to do real science."*

## The Theranos Internal Culture & Red Flags
* **Extreme Secrecy and Paranoia:**
    * The company operated under intense silos, overreaching non-disclosure agreements, and heavy turnover.
    * Employees received virtually zero stock options, relying instead on visas, mortgages, and student debt to stay.
* **The Launch and Lab Reality:**
    * Joined full-time on the exact day Theranos launched its retail product at Walgreens in Palo Alto, during which the assay validation manager quit after a screaming match with Sunny Balwani.
    * Discovered that zero tests were validated on the proprietary Theranos platform; instead, patient samples were run on third-party commercial equipment bought from Siemens and Roche, or outsourced entirely.
* **Toxic Leadership:**
    * Sunny Balwani managed the lab through bullying, fear, and intimidation, pushing employees to run patient samples despite quality control failures.
    * Elizabeth Holmes cultivated an angelic public persona as a visionary healthcare darling while allowing Sunny to run the internal operations with a "mob boss" mentality.

## Whistleblowing & Internal Resistance
* **Escalating Concerns:**
    * Uncovered severe failures during assay validations, notably a syphilis test displaying unacceptable 65% sensitivity and over 20% false positives among employees.
    * Reached out anonymously to the New York State Department of Health, confirming that Theranos's audit cheating methods violated federal and state regulations.
* **Internal Pushback:**
    * Gently raised technical and ethical concerns to Elizabeth Holmes and a vice president, only to be stonewalled, ignored, and gaslit.
    * Emailed a detailed breakdown of observations and data to Holmes, which was forwarded to Sunny Balwani. Balwani responded with a blistering all-red, all-caps attack calling Tyler arrogant, ignorant, and threatening him.
* **Resignation:**
    * Submitted a two-week notice, successfully sneaking out a ream of printed email threads hidden under a sweatshirt on his last day.

## The Legal Campaign & Intimidation
* **The Grandfather Dynamic:**
    * George Shultz, a Theranos board member with a massive percentage of his net worth tied up in exclusive Theranos stock (including a trust fund for Tyler's future children), was heavily manipulated and initially refused to believe the warnings.
* **Boies Schiller Ambush:**
    * Summoned to his grandfather's house under the guise of signing a one-page non-disclosure agreement, Tyler was instead ambushed by lawyers from David Boies's firm bearing a Temporary Restraining Order (TRO), an affidavit demanding the names of other sources, and a court appearance notice.
    * Stalled the legal pressure by demanding legal counsel and eventually secured top-tier specialized legal representation, spending $400,000 to $500,000 in legal fees.
* **Surveillance and Fear:**
    * Endured months of intimidation, including being followed by private investigators and experiencing severe psychological stress and isolation.

## Vindication & Public Exposure
* **Going on the Record:**
    * Connected with Wall Street Journal reporter John Carreyrou, providing background information and the core phrase: *"Fraud is not a trade secret."*
    * Formally went on the record in October 2015 as part of Carreyrou's investigative series, dismantling Theranos's public facade and triggering inspections by CMS and the FDA.
* **Happy Resolution:**
    * Despite initial friction, repaired relations with his parents and eventually reconnected with a former college housemate in Boston, leading to marriage and starting a family.

## Notable Quotes
> *"Elizabeth Holmes was the type of person where as soon as she starts speaking, the rest of the room would just go silent. Like she had this way of just locking in an audience. And when she spoke to you, she made you feel like you were the most important person in her entire world in that moment."*
> — Tyler Shultz

> *"When management knows they're being watched, they know that they need that they cannot give the result of a Theranos test because the regulator will know that the answer is wrong... but if it was an unsuspecting patient who walked into Walgreens, they were perfectly comfortable knowingly giving them incorrect medical information."*
> — Tyler Shultz

> *"Why on earth would I want that [trust fund] to go to zero? Like I want that to be worth something... I don't want it to be an excuse for aiding and abetting a fraud... I have no motivation to bring this company down. I would be so happy to be wrong."*
> — Tyler Shultz

> *"Fraud is not a trade secret."*
> — Tyler Shultz

items.title: Mike Milken: Who Gets Access to Capital? | Podcast | In Good Company
items.summary: Mike Milken, pioneer of the high-yield bond market, discusses how a chance encounter at age 19 shaped his lifelong mission to expand access to capital, drive medical research, and foster upward mobility.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Mike Milken, pioneer of the high-yield bond market, discusses how a chance encounter at age 19 shaped his lifelong mission to expand access to capital, drive medical research, and foster upward mobility. Joined by host Nicolai Tangen, they explore the realities of modern credit markets, human capital, and the global shifts in entrepreneurship.

## High-Yield Bonds and the Evolution of Credit Markets
* **Genesis at Age 19:**
  * **Catalyst Event:** **Mike Milken** met a young African American man at the August 11, 1965 Watts Riots in Los Angeles who stated he lacked access to capital because of the color of his skin.
  * **Research Discovery:** Milken studied credit history at Berkeley and discovered that Great Depression data proved lower-quality debt yielded higher risk-adjusted returns, while sovereign debt carried the highest historical risk despite AAA ratings.
* **Overcoming Institutional Resistance:**
  * **Drexel's Transition:** Milken utilized multiple-choice questions and comparative tests (showing buy-recommendation stocks had non-investment grade debt while sells had investment grade debt) to guide colleagues toward self-discovery.
  * **The 1974 Turning Point:** When the stock market dropped 50% and interest rates doubled, straight non-investment grade debt generated 100% returns between late 1974 and 1976, waking up skeptics.
* **Financing New Industries:**
  * **Pioneered Sectors:** High-yield capital built the energy industry, biotech, cable, home building, hospitality/casinos (e.g., Mirage), and telecommunications.
  * **MCI Telecom Impact:** Long-distance phone calls cost $10/minute in the 1970s; financing MCI helped reduce costs by 75%, laying groundwork for modern digital communication.
  * **Job Creation Impact:** In the last 30 years of the 20th century, non-investment grade companies created over 60 million jobs in the US, compared to minus 4 million created by investment grade companies.

## Human Capital, Wealth, and Global Shifts
* **Valuation of Human vs. Financial Assets:**
  * **Gary Becker's Concept:** Milken applied Nobel laureate Gary Becker's human capital framework, noting that US human and social capital is valued at over **$2,000 trillion**, dwarfing financial assets at roughly **$300 trillion** and US GDP of around **$30 trillion**.
* **Global Wealth Migration:**
  * **Millionaire Destinations:** In 2023–2024, the UAE became the top global destination for millionaires, followed by the US in second and Singapore in third.
  * **Domestic Shifts:** Entrepreneurs like Elon Musk (SpaceX moving to Texas) and Alex Karp (Palantir moving headquarters to Florida) highlight massive state-to-state and international shifts in job creation and capital.
* **The American Dream Center:**
  * **Washington DC Initiative:** Opened in September near the White House, the center serves as a beacon of hope for the one-third of the population doubting upward mobility, anchored by four pillars: education, healthcare, financial literacy, and finding new entrepreneurs.

## Private Credit, Systemic Risks, and Lessons from Drexel
* **Private Credit vs. Public Credit:**
  * **Nature of the Market:** Milken views private credit as largely similar to public non-investment grade debt, functioning as a throwback to 1950s/1960s insurance company lending.
  * **Fee Structure:** Money managers charge 3 to 5 times more to manage money in private credit, creating strong internal incentives.
* **Maturity Mismatches:**
  * **Banking Failures:** Silicon Valley Bank and Republic Bank failed not due to asset credit quality, but from financing intermediate US government securities and long-term assets with overnight/short-term liabilities during surging interest rates.
* **The Drexel Legacy:**
  * **Alumni Success:** Former Drexel colleagues who went on to lead firms like Apollo (e.g., Tony Ressler) and Ares, or Goldman Sachs, retained a core belief in financing people and ideas first.
  * **Changing Motivations:** In the 1970s, 25% of finance entrants stated they wanted to "change the world"; today, incoming classes see that drop to roughly 1% due to massive compensation inflation.

## Medical Research, Longevity, and Motivation
* **Economic Impact of Healthcare:**
  * **Life Expectancy Gains:** Global average life expectancy rose from 31 years in 1900 to the mid-70s today through antibiotics and public health advancements.
  * **Growth Driver:** Milken notes that more than 50% of all global economic growth has come from advances in healthcare and public health.
* **Personal Drivers at Age 80:**
  * **Family Perspective:** 97% of Milken's efforts are focused on the world his grandchildren will inherit, driven by his father's early lesson that everyone must feel they have a chance to succeed.

## Notable Quotes
> *"The truth was there was research that was done... it showed that during the worldwide depression of the '30s that the highest rate of return was the lower quality of the debt you bought. In other words, the risk premiums were too large."*
> — **Mike Milken**

> *"In the last 30 years of the 20th century, more than 60 million jobs were created... by non-investment grade companies and minus 4 million jobs were created by investment grade companies."*
> — **Mike Milken**

> *"People talk a lot about economics, but if you really study more than 50% of all economic growth in the world has come from advances in healthcare and public health."*
> — **Mike Milken**

items.title: Mike Volpi on Why AI Infrastructure Will Outlast the Hype Cycle
items.summary: The AI infrastructure buildout shares structural parallels with the late-1990s internet boom, but the economic value of intelligence exceeds that of communication, and GPUs are proving to have a longer useful life than anticipated.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
The AI infrastructure buildout shares structural parallels with the late-1990s internet boom, but the economic value of intelligence exceeds that of communication, and GPUs are proving to have a longer useful life than anticipated. While an economic correction is likely for weaker neo-clouds, the underlying infrastructure assets will remain highly valuable over the long term.

## The AI Infrastructure Buildout vs. the 1990s Internet Boom
* **Historical Parallels:** Mike Volpi compares today’s AI investment to the late '90s fiber-optic boom, noting that history "doesn't repeat itself, but it definitely rhymes." Both eras featured high expectations of transformative societal impact, parallel surges in demand, and massive influxes of debt and equity capital.
* **Technology & Demand Differences:** 
  * **Bandwidth vs. Compute:** Fiber capacity grew exponentially through WDM (adding colors of light to fiber), whereas compute is bound by a more moderated pace resembling Moore's Law.
  * **Revenue Adoption:** Model providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, open-source model providers like Fireworks, Together, and Model) are experiencing revenue ramps far superior to the internet bandwidth providers of the '90s.
  * **Scale:** The current AI buildout represents roughly 2% of global GDP, reflecting a larger macroeconomic investment because it builds "intelligence" rather than mere communication.
* **Asset Longevity & Scarcity:** 
  * **GPU Useful Life:** Despite expectations that Hopper (H100) chips would approach obsolescence after a few years, severe manufacturing scarcity has kept them fully utilized at high rental rates ($2.50 to $3.00/hour).
  * **Token Efficiency:** The ultimate metric is token revenue per watt. Newer architectures (Blackwell, Vera Rubin) convert electricity to dollars more efficiently, but extreme scarcity keeps older generations in demand.
  * **Bankruptcies & Asset Reuse:** Similar to how '90s fiber networks survived provider bankruptcies to serve future utility, today's compute assets will be fully utilized long-term, though ownership may shift if weaker neo-clouds collapse.

## Enterprise M&A Playbook: Lessons from Cisco and Nvidia
* **Cisco’s M&A Strategy:** During Volpi's tenure starting in 1994, Cisco completed roughly 70 acquisitions, which eventually accounted for 50% of the company's $30 billion in revenue. 
  * **Statistical Success:** Cisco maintained a risk-tolerant model where roughly one-third of acquisitions succeeded wildly, one-third performed moderately, and one-third failed. 
  * **Valuation & Currency:** Most deals were all-equity transactions capped at 4% to 5% of Cisco's market cap. Networking acquisitions integrated rapidly because they relied on open protocols (OSPF, BGP, Ethernet).
* **Nvidia's Strategic Position:** 
  * **Aggressive Expansion:** Nvidia has acquired foundational assets like Mellanox (the world's largest networking company) and taken equity/financing stakes in ~200 neo-clouds to shape industry structure and avoid disintermediation by a handful of hyperscalers.
  * **The Limits of Industry Shaping:** Volpi notes that industries dominated by scale economies (like the 3 major hyperscalers or airlines) naturally consolidate; funding weaker startups/neo-clouds is a noble effort for innovation, but ultimately futile against natural market consolidation.
* **Integration Best Practices:** Guido Appenzeller and Mike Volpi agree that post-acquisition integration requires rigid, centralized repeatable processes rather than treating integration as an ad-hoc one-time event. Larger acquisitions (such as Cisco's purchase of Scientific Atlanta) suffer from severe cultural and operational friction.

## Semiconductor Technology, Silicon, and Architecture
* **System-Level Architecture:** 
  * **Monolithic vs. Patchwork:** Modern AI workloads require treating the entire infrastructure as a single system. Google's TPU architecture represents the gold standard of system-level design, whereas mixing disparate chips (e.g., Cerebras with Arista switches) introduces architectural inefficiencies.
  * **The Rack as a Unit:** The minimum deployable unit has shifted from individual cards to entire racks (such as Nvidia's Blackwell configurations) and whole data-center rows (utilizing optical circuit switching).
* **Silicon Evolution & Memory Constraints:** 
  * **Diversity in Chip Design:** As model architectures diversify (FP4, FP8, mixture of experts, varying parameter counts), silicon diversity will increase through hardware-software co-design.
  * **Reasoning Intensity:** Reasoning-driven AI workloads require large parameter counts and massive KV caches, heavily favoring architectures with high memory bandwidth (such as 3D DRAM and hybrid copper bonding).
  * **Packaging Challenges:** Integrating logic and memory chips into the same package introduces severe thermal management hurdles due to differing heat profiles.

## Networking: The Innovator's Dilemma in Data Centers
* **The Death of Statistical Multiplexing:** Traditional data center networking (Broadcom Tomahawk/Dune architectures) relies on stochastic packet switching (stat-muxing variable-length IP packets), designed for unpredictable internet traffic patterns.
* **Predictable AI Workloads:** AI training and batch-inference workloads feature continuous, highly predictable, fully utilized traffic flows. 
* **The Need for Circuit Switching:** Volpi argues that the future of data center networking will shift away from expensive, complex stat-muxed packet switches toward optical circuit switches, Time Division Multiplexing (TDM), or MEMS-based systems—posing a classic innovator's dilemma for legacy networking vendors.

## Portfolio Strategy and Founder M&A Advice
* **Evaluating Exit Options:** When advising startup boards on acquisition offers, founders must evaluate whether the leadership team has the "fire" to push through to the next phase, and whether the business has a realistic path to 10x growth rather than just doubling.
* **Continuous Intelligence Gathering:** Volpi advises founders to reject passive inbound acquisition offers (which usually indicate an auction or a missed window) and instead maintain an ongoing dialogue with competitors and major players (Nvidia, Amazon, OpenAI) through regular coffee meetings as an "inverse intelligence gathering mechanism."

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Mike Volpi predicts** there will be an economic correction and cleaning up of the industry structure affecting weaker neo-cloud balance sheets.
* **Mike Volpi predicts** that fab capacity constraints will persist, meaning the semiconductor manufacturing bottleneck will not change significantly over the next 2 to 3 years, and potentially up to 5 years out.
* **Mike Volpi predicts** that data center networking architectures will eventually abandon stochastic stat-muxed packet switching in favor of predictable circuit-switched or optical designs.

## Notable Quotes
> *"History doesn't repeat itself, but it definitely rhymes."*  
> — **Mike Volpi**

> *"If your stock trades more than the price you paid for the acquisition in one day, then you can do the acquisitions as many as you want. Nobody will care."*  
> — **Mike Volpi**

> *"The industry wants to look a certain way because when it does it creates maximum utility, maximum economic value... You can fund 100 airlines in America, but in the end you're going to have three."*  
> — **Mike Volpi**

items.title: What Comes After Loops?: Deep Dive Into Agentic Architecture | DevDay 2026
items.summary: OpenAI engineers Raj Bhatek and Eric traced the evolution of AI agents from simple prompt-response loops to collaborative, multi-agent systems—culminating in a massive 10,000-agent architecture that successfully tackled the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem.
items.content_text:
- **TL;DR:** OpenAI engineers Raj Bhatek and Eric traced the evolution of AI agents from simple prompt-response loops to collaborative, multi-agent systems—culminating in a massive 10,000-agent architecture that successfully tackled the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem.

## Evolution of Agentic Architecture: From Loops to Codex
- **Initial Paradigm Shift:** 
  - Early AI interactions required manual human intervention (e.g., copying and pasting code like FizzBuzz).
  - The introduction of reasoning combined with tool use (such as in the o3 launch) created the foundational "agentic loop."
- **The Codex General Agent:**
  - Built as a union of a model and a harness working together; OpenAI open-sourced Codex with a minimal, opinionated design giving models access to a computer via shell, file system, and computer use.
  - The **Responses API** manages the tool-call loop, execution sandbox, and conversation context.
- **Solving Long-Horizon Work via Compaction:**
  - Early models hit context window limits and stopped prematurely.
  - OpenAI trained **native compaction** into both the harness and model (accessible via the `/compact` endpoint in the Responses API), allowing models to resume from a condensed state and handle multi-window tasks.
- **From Outer Loops to Native Persistence:**
  - Developers initially used manual scripts or brute-force loops (like Geoffrey Huntley's "Ralph loop" or using `continue` statements) to keep models working.
  - Introduced `--goal` in GPT-5.5 to track objectives outside the core context window.
  - With GPT-5.6, persistence was trained directly into the model, eliminating the need for `--goal` hacks. Wharton professor Ethan Mullica notably tested this by having Codex play *Slay the Spire 2* for five hours straight.

## Multi-Agent Workflows & Best Practices
- **Scaling from Single Agents:**
  - Eric (DX team) advises starting with a single agent and clear verification methods for tasks before scaling up to teams.
- **Autonomous Coordination (GPT-6):**
  - GPT-6 series models can coordinate and collaborate natively, breaking down massive tasks (like full codebase refactors or game ports) by spinning up subagents (e.g., Ultra) autonomously.
- **Agent Geometries and Effort Scaling:**
  - **Effort Scaling:** Dynamically assigns reasoning effort and models using subagents (e.g., Sol managing integration, Astra handling difficult test failures, and Luna taking on simple busy work).
  - **The Pair Pattern:** Deploying a pair of subagents with explicit communication boundaries (e.g., one agent handling capture tech in an old game engine, the other unpacking/visualizing the scene in Blender).
  - **Thread Managers:** Using ChatGPT app threads to spin up and manage separate conversations for discrete tasks (like a separate chat for every PR in a review queue) while keeping the manager informed.
  - **Departmental Roles:** Structuring long-running projects (like video games) by assigning agents distinct lanes (art director, playtester, programmer, producer).
- **Pitfalls to Avoid:**
  - **Middle Management Tax:** Overcomplicating agent hierarchies with too many rules causes agents to stall seeking approval.
  - **Context Drift & The Work Log:** To counteract short-term memory loss and constant human nagging/steering, prompt Codex to maintain a compact work log containing the overall goal, running work, and how recent steering relates to both.

## Scaling to the Next Generation: Agent Teams
- **Massive-Scale Collaboration:**
  - Moving beyond a handful of agents to thousands (e.g., 10,000 agents) to tackle massive, complex problems.
- **The Navier-Stokes Breakthrough:**
  - OpenAI utilized an internal advanced model alongside Codex to solve the long-standing Millennium Prize Navier-Stokes problem using **10,000 agents**, generating **2.7 million messages** and **130 billion output tokens**.
- **Agent Team Architecture:**
  - **Unified Goal with Diversity:** Initialized multiple teams with different versions of a problem to encourage varied approaches and prevent duplicative effort.
  - **Cross-Team Communication:** Agents share findings and ask questions across different teams.
  - **Dynamic Orchestration:** As hypotheses were explored and new questions arose, teams were dynamically created, steered, or redirected toward promising lines (e.g., all teams being diverted to the unforced Euler result once found).
  - **Broader Impact:** Using this internal model architecture, OpenAI resolved more than **100 longstanding problems** across mathematics and continues making discoveries in math and science.

## Notable Quotes
> "As models get better, things change. How we build them really does, too."
> — Raj Bhatek

> "Every agent Codex brings in can dramatically increase token use without necessarily making the work faster or better. It's up to you to decide when a problem needs the extra help."
> — Eric

> "Try not to overthink managing all your agents. It's just often not worth the hassle, and it makes it very easy to lose track of how complex your agent teams have gotten."
> — Eric

items.title: You’re probably sleepwalking through life (here's how to wake up) - Robert Greene
items.summary: Author Robert Greene joins hosts Shaan Puri and Sam Parr on Episode 881 of My First Million to discuss his new book The Law of the Sublime, the crisis of modern smartphone addiction, and the necessity of stepping outside to reconnect with agency, awe, and human nature.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Author Robert Greene joins hosts Shaan Puri and Sam Parr on Episode 881 of My First Million to discuss his new book *The Law of the Sublime*, the crisis of modern smartphone addiction, and the necessity of stepping outside to reconnect with agency, awe, and human nature.

## The Modern Malaise: Technology, Addiction, and Disconnection
- **Smartphone Addiction:** 
  - **Ubiquity:** 90%+ of American adults have a smartphone, and an estimated 90%+ of those users are addicted to them, spending roughly 7 hours a day on the device.
  - **Erosion of Agency:** Algorithms on Instagram, X, and TikTok program users' thoughts, feelings, and experiences, driving a deep, modern sense of powerlessness.
- **Situational Blindness:** 
  - **Externalized Focus:** People walk through beautiful natural settings like Los Angeles parks staring at their phones, which Greene characterizes as a form of mental illness.
  - **Atrophied Brains:** Easy, instantaneous gratification is rewiring the human brain, breeding a generation that lacks the patience to read a 400-page book or write an essay.

## The Path to Reconnection: The Sublime and Inner Agency
- **Breaking the Cycle:** 
  - **Cold Turkey Withdrawal:** Leave the phone behind, lock it in a drawer, and go outside into nature where you are forced to interact with the non-human world.
  - **Awe and Scale:** Activities like climbing a mountain break people out of the tiny circle imposed by technology and restore a sense of wonder.
- **The Limits of External Stimulation:** 
  - **The Flatness Trap:** Constantly chasing external distractions leaves individuals feeling empty because the restless human mind immediately demands more.
  - **Internal Fulfillment:** True, lasting fulfillment comes from within—through physical adventure, love, or connecting with animals—experiences that cannot be programmed by a phone.

## Historical Resilience and the Power of Purpose
- **The Andes Plane Crash (1971):** 
  - **Extreme Survival:** Uruguayan rugby players trapped in the 14,000-foot Andes mountains with no winter gear or climbing equipment survived by drawing on deep internal resources.
  - **The Power of Will:** Nando Parado climbed a vertical wall of ice and rock with improvised tools for two hours out of love and a sense of purpose to return to his father.
- **Viktor Frankl & Concentration Camp Survival:** 
  - **Meaning as Survival:** In Auschwitz, survivors were overwhelmingly those who had a distinct purpose, such as a book to write or a family member to save.

## Mastering Power, Mystery, and Charisma
- **Core Lessons from *The 48 Laws of Power*:** 
  - **Say Less Than Necessary:** In the social media era, people reveal too much; power requires a balance of absence and presence.
  - **Disappear:** Celebrities like Beyoncé disappear for a year and a half before dropping a record, letting speculation build an air of mystery.
- **The Psychology of Charisma:** 
  - **Childhood Trauma Origin:** Many charismatic figures (e.g., Marilyn Monroe, Malcolm X) come from deeply troubled or abandoned backgrounds, making them outerdirected and desperate for public love.
  - **Confidence as a Core Trait:** True charisma stems from inner security and an intense drive behind a cause, whereas fake confidence reads as empty bravado.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **AI and Legal Professions:** AI will "decimate" the legal profession because individuals will be able to get answers to any legal problem instantly, as stated by Robert Greene.
- **AI and Negative Human Nature:** The dark side of human nature (irrationality, grandiosity, phishing, scams, and the creation of biological weapons/dirty bombs) will increasingly hijack AI technology over the coming years, according to Robert Greene.
- **AI and Public Resentment:** Deep wells of public resentment and fear regarding AI will eventually force political movements to demand strict laws capping data centers and regulating the technology, predicted by Robert Greene.

## Notable Quotes
> "People are suffering from the narrowness of their experience. A lot of it coming from technology. There's something incredible about just simply being alive."
> — Robert Greene

> "There's no experience that could be programmed on your stupid phone that can ever give you that kind of sensation... I did something difficult, arduous, but I feel wow look at this."
> — Robert Greene

> "Power is about absence and presence. If you're always present, people take you for granted... grow bored with you. If you're always absent, you have there's nothing to talk about."
> — Robert Greene

> "I just make what's cool to me and sometimes the whole world agrees."
> — Mike Posner (cited by Shaan Puri)

items.title: Alex Karp on Why AI Will Hurt the Middle Class: You Can’t Have Billionaires Becoming 100x Wealthier
items.summary: Alex Karp argues that unchecked AI and massive wealth concentration will widen class divides, threatening American democracy unless tech, government, and society realign to protect human dignity, civil liberties, and the working class.
items.content_text:
### TL;DR
Alex Karp argues that unchecked AI and massive wealth concentration will widen class divides, threatening American democracy unless tech, government, and society realign to protect human dignity, civil liberties, and the working class.

## The Outsider Mindset & Palantir's Origins
* **Dyslexia as a Cognitive Advantage:** 
  * Alex Karp attributes his ability to build unconventional software to his dyslexia, defining it as a non-one-to-one relationship with written language taxonomy.
  * Being dyslexic prevented him from being "colonized by the broader culture," allowing him to interact with technology and real-world problems objectively.
* **Rejecting Silicon Valley Norms:** 
  * Palantir operated for roughly three years without revenue to build a high-value anti-terror product rather than a simple, addictive consumer app.
  * Karp spent years studying Martin Heidegger's philosophy and its influence on modern regressive political movements before co-founding Palantir with Peter Thiel.
* **The Genesis of Palantir:** 
  * Inspired by PayPal's fraud-identification software, Peter Thiel approached Karp during their time at Stanford Law School to bring similar data-connecting methodologies to the intelligence space.

## Surveillance, National Security, and Privacy
* **Balancing Security and Civil Liberties:** 
  * Palantir’s products are utilized in Europe and the U.S. to dismantle organized criminal gangs, stop border-enforcement trafficking, and prevent terrorist attacks under strict legal mandates and warrants.
  * Karp warns that failing to stop these threats would give rise to far-left or far-right fascism, resulting in total domestic surveillance.
* **Commercial vs. Government Overreach:** 
  * Karp argues that citizens over-index on fearing government surveillance while ignoring commercial data collection by tech companies that heavily influence human thought and opinions.
  * He advocates for strict legislation to restrict battlefield AI technologies from being deployed domestically.

## Wealth Disparity, Capitalism, and the Middle Class
* **The Dangerous Fracturing of Society:** 
  * Karp asserts that billionaires becoming 100x wealthier while the middle class and working class see marginal gains breaks the tacit covenant between wealth creation and societal value.
  * AI will exacerbate these disparities, creating extreme wealth for tech elites while leaving working-class vocational workers behind.
* **Flaws of Proposed Solutions:** 
  * A traditional wealth tax is impractical, fails to help the poor, breaks tech culture liquidity, and inherently requires invasive surveillance to assess asset values.
  * **Karp's Taxation Compromise:** Proposes raising taxes on the wealthy *only* under the condition that every unit of tax raised is matched by half a unit of identified government waste, directly funding programs that improve working-class lives without destroying the tech ecosystem.

## Silicon Valley, National Sovereignty, and Enterprise AI
* **The Broken Social Contract:** 
  * Silicon Valley is described as a "highly insulated island" that has lost touch with mainstream America, producing ads and consumerism while generating anti-government sentiment.
  * Despite this, Karp notes that the U.S. military—the only indisputably noble institution in the eyes of most Americans—remains the foundational hybrid of government, Stanford academia, and venture capital that birthed the valley.
* **Enterprise Backlash Against LLMs:** 
  * U.S. enterprises are enraged and apoplectic because they are paying high fees for Large Language Models while unknowingly having their proprietary data used to train models that ultimately compete against them.
  * Palantir combats this by providing "ontologies"—contextual frameworks that act as an alpha creator and a protective layer, allowing enterprises to interact with open and closed AI models safely and securely.

## What It Means to Be Human
* **The Challenge of Artificial Superintelligence:** 
  * As AI surpasses human cognitive abilities—long considered the core capacity underlying moral systems and claims of superiority—society faces the question of what makes humans special.
* **The Radical Protection of the Constitution:** 
  * Karp emphasizes that the U.S. Constitution uniquely frames rights as granted by a higher figure, rooting human value in something above and beyond mere cognitive skill.
  * This foundational belief protects the artistic, individual, and particular nature of humanity, making the defense of American constitutional order vital in the age of intelligent machines.

---

## Notable Quotes
> "The biggest norm we violated is it took three years really roughly without revenue. Three years, no revenue. You would have to be basically insane to do that. And I do think it took a neurodivergent person at the helm to fight for that."
> — Alex Karp

> "You can't have people becoming a hundred times wealthier when they're already billionaires and everyone else is becoming 5% wealthier, okay? So that's legitimate."
> — Alex Karp

> "The valley was built as a hybrid basically university, government, capital."
> — Alex Karp

items.title: Amazon AWS CEO: AI boom is just getting started
items.summary: AWS CEO Matt Garman explains how the AI boom is accelerating Amazon's cloud business toward a potential $1 trillion revenue run rate by driving core on-premise workloads into the cloud.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
AWS CEO Matt Garman explains how the AI boom is accelerating Amazon's cloud business toward a potential $1 trillion revenue run rate by driving core on-premise workloads into the cloud. Despite adding one GPU every 14 seconds, AWS anticipates severe capacity shortages for the next couple of years.

## AWS Growth & The AI-Driven Cloud Migration
* **Accelerating On-Premise Migration:** 
  * AI agents require access to all enterprise data sources, forcing companies to migrate legacy workloads (mainframes, VMware clusters, on-prem databases) into the cloud.
