items.title: The Future of AI Is Absolutely Incredible (Spencer Huang)
items.summary: Physical AI is significantly more difficult than text-based LLMs due to the absence of a pre-existing physical data record and the complex, bidirectional coupling of the real world.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Physical AI is significantly more difficult than text-based LLMs due to the absence of a pre-existing physical data record and the complex, bidirectional coupling of the real world. Overcoming this requires hybrid training architectures that combine conventional physics simulators, neural world models, and high-performance hardware.

## Announcements and Platform Ecosystem
* **Isaac Lab & Newton Updates:** **Spencer Huang** announced updates to Isaac Lab integrating the Newton physics framework (moving away from PhysX) to provide developer quality-of-life improvements and better scaling capabilities.
* **DGX Station Blueprints:** Released as a starting point for training robotic policies directly on desk-ready workstations.
* **Agile One SN Reference Platform:** Built alongside Agile, featuring out-of-the-box integration with Thor, optimized firmware/software stacks, pre-configured Groot, and Uji hands to eliminate weeks or months of integration friction.

## Why Physical AI Is Fundamentally Harder Than LLMs
* **Lack of Historical Data:** **Spencer Huang** noted that while LLMs benefited from centuries of written and recorded human history, no comparable dataset encapsulates the physics and interactions of the physical world.
* **Bidirectional Coupling:** Unlike text, physical robots manipulate the world and the world manipulates back, creating complex deformations and forces that require robust physics solvers.
* **Teleop and Data Collection Bottlenecks:** Teleoperation is uniquely difficult due to a lack of force feedback (comparable to numbing one's hands), though recent advancements leverage egocentric and human-pose data alongside imitation learning.

## The Ideal Data Diet and Hybrid Simulation
* **Conventional vs. Neural Simulators:** **Spencer Huang** explained that conventional simulators provide grounded, reliable physics but are tedious to build and lack diversity. Neural simulators (world models like Cosmos) offer vast diversity and multi-modality (tactile, acoustics, force feedback) but can hallucinate physics if not properly anchored.
* **Automatic Domain Randomization:** Using neural simulators to randomize materials, lighting, and deformations while feeding them through a conventional physics-backed environment creates a hybridized training diet.
* **Sensitivity Analysis and Failure-Based Learning:** Policies are tested inside Isaac Lab arenas, where tasks are decomposed into subtasks to isolate failures (such as collisions or lighting issues) and enable iterative, human-like failure recovery.

## Whole-Body Control and Small-Scale Models
* **Sonic Model (42M Parameters):** **Spencer Huang** highlighted Sonic as an open-weight, open-access model that achieves whole-body control for tracking, walking, crawling, and dancing across different body morphologies using only 42 million parameters.
* **System Hierarchy:** Low-level models like Sonic handle rapid "System Zero" reactions (staying upright, rapid stepping), while Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models handle long-horizon reasoning.
* **Whole-Body Maneuvers:** Whole-body control bridges the gap between lower and upper body actions, allowing robots to walk and manipulate simultaneously (such as walking while carrying a heavy box or holding a cup).

## The Sim-to-Real Gap and Real-World Adaptation
* **The "Doomed to Succeed" Phenomenon:** **Spencer Huang** warned that developers are often doomed to succeed in simulation because parameters can always be tuned to fit a virtual environment without guaranteeing zero-shot real-world transfer.
* **End-to-End Nature of the Gap:** The sim-to-real gap is not a single phase but spans data collection, kinematic mapping (retargeting human data to robot joints), training configurations, and deployment evaluation.
* **Emergent Failure Recovery:** With sufficient training and simulation across envelopes, models exhibit emergent behaviors—such as robot dogs or humanoids adapting to walk on three working legs or a slightly broken ankle joint.

## Notable Quotes
> "The goal is to get more work done... The less friction the better."
> — **Spencer Huang**

> "We like to say that you're doomed to succeed in simulation... because no matter no matter what you can always tune something to have it succeed in simulation."
> — **Spencer Huang**

> "At no point have we gotten lazier. We've actually just found more ways to make ourselves, you know, push the frontiers of of automation."
> — **Spencer Huang**

items.title: The Hidden Capital Crunch Behind Silicon Valley’s AI Boom
items.summary: Silicon Valley venture capital is experiencing unprecedented velocity and multi-billion-dollar funding rounds driven by the explosive growth of AI, where startups now target trillion-dollar outcomes and face massive capital demands primarily driven by compute.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Silicon Valley venture capital is experiencing unprecedented velocity and multi-billion-dollar funding rounds driven by the explosive growth of AI, where startups now target trillion-dollar outcomes and face massive capital demands primarily driven by compute. Abstract Ventures Managing Partner Ramtin Naimi and host Patrick discuss how this market differs from 2021 through structural shifts in valuations, venture fund deployment pacing, and liquidity crunches.

## Deal-Level Dynamics & The Venture Frenzy
- **Insane Deal Velocity:** Rounds and follow-on financings are happening faster than ever, with top-tier founders commanding intense investor demand and preferential pricing.
- **The "Cuck Tranche":** When investors lose out on a primary round, instead of waiting for a later stage, many are paying 3x to 5x higher valuations in tandem with the primary round to secure secondary access.
- **Revenue Nuances:** While companies report 10x to 20x year-over-year growth, revenues often carry caveats such as low or negative margins, high customer concentration, annualized figures from short-term data sales, or usage-based consumer models rather than pure SaaS metrics.
- **Margin Expansion:** Conversely, foundation model providers and portfolio companies are seeing rapid margin improvements; Anthropic reported 85% gross margins in the first half of the year, while some portfolio companies are scaling revenue 200% to 700% while margins shift from -15% to +35%.

## Market Comparison: Today vs. 2021
- **Similarities:** Both eras feature rapid capital deployment, intense FOMO, and late-stage public market crossover investors pushing aggressively into venture deals. Abstract Ventures observed a recent uptick in term sheets being renegotiated or pulled after being offered, reminiscent of late 2021.
- **Differences in Quality & Pace:** Unlike 2021—where companies had constrained TAMs, modest 3x–5x SAS growth, and required a 7-year timeline to reach $100M ARR—today's companies are finding product-market fit at record speeds and driving tangible value that everyday consumers and families actively integrate into daily life.

## The Venture Fund Capital Crunch & LP Liquidity
- **Accelerated Deployment:** Mega platform funds modeled for 18-to-24-month deployment windows are returning to market 3x faster because they severely underestimated the capital required to secure target ownership percentages at higher company valuations.
- **Example Fund Pacing:** One fund raised $2.5 billion, started deploying in July, and scheduled a return to market by January; another fund deployed $3 billion over 9 months and returned seeking $5 billion.
- **Funding Delays:** For the first time in this cycle, VCs issuing term sheets (e.g., a $150M commitment or a $40M-out-of-$50M commitment) are asking founders to wait several months for funding while they close new funds and set up capital call facilities.
- **LP Liquidity Bottlenecks:** Traditional LPs (endowments and foundations) expected much higher liquidity by now. Meaningful liquidity is heavily concentrated in just a few massive names—SpaceX, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Databricks—meaning LPs lacking exposure to these specific companies are facing cash constraints.

## Compute Demands and Financing Challenges
- **The NeoCloud Landscape:** While hyperscalers and frontier model labs drive the bulk of compute demand, roughly 80 to 90 NeoClouds have raised $1 billion to $5 billion. One NeoCloud met by Abstract was raising a $1 billion round to spend entirely on compute for a single training run, projecting another $5柏 billion needed over the next year.
- **Benchmark Maxing vs. Commercial Viability:** It is increasingly difficult to discern whether new model launches are genuinely groundbreaking at scale or simply "benchmark-maxed" to perform well on standardized tests without immediate commercial viability.
- **Alternative Financing Structures:** Companies like General Catalyst offer customer value funds, and some VCs are exploring financing startups with compute resources instead of cash. However, equity dilution remains preferred due to the complexities of compute longevity and the avoidance of restrictive debt covenants.

## Seed Strategy: Proactive vs. Reactive Investing
- **Goalpost Shift:** Terminal outcome expectations have shifted from $10 billion (2016) to $100 billion (2021) to $1-trillion outcomes today, led by OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceX (with Naimi predicting 2 to 3 more, not 40).
- **Proactive Alpha:** Reactive investors who chased obvious consensus assets (like 100x SaaS multiples in 2021) underperformed. Proactive investors who back exceptional founders working on non-obvious markets generate outsized alpha.
- **Case Study — Conduit:** Seeded 9 months ago in Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI) via a non-invasive head-worn device achieving 80% thought accuracy with small training data. After hitting 30,000 hours of training data, BCI became a hot category, leading to a heavily oversubscribed round with 13 term sheets.
- **Case Study — Etched:** Despite widespread VC skepticism that a startup could out-compete chip fabrication incumbents, Sequoia's $10 billion valuation validation proved founders can run circles around incumbents before markets recognize the trend.

## Evolution of Abstract Ventures
- **Fund Scaling:** Abstract's Fund I in 2018 was $100 million (viewed by LPs as too large for a debut fund), while their latest vintage is $800 million (viewed as disciplined).
- **Moving Up-Stack:** Abstract has expanded from pure seed to leading Series B financings (e.g., Socket, Doctronic, Dust), making passive growth investments (e.g., Crusoe), and allocating 15% of their 2023 vintage into XAI's formation round and participating in Polymarket's Series B.

## Notable Quotes
> *"The round structures, the volume of deals, people feeling the need that they need to keep up with the market is all very similar... But the thing that's most dissimilar is kind of the enthusiasm around the companies. I don't think people were investing in companies in 2021 thinking that these companies were going to be category defining or be global scale companies within 18 to 24 months."* — Ramtin Naimi
> 
> *"If you are at the early stages at least, if you're backing great founders working on obviously good ideas, you're going to pay sky-high market pricing... But if you back great founders working on non-obvious ideas, that generally tends to be the best way to generate alpha in markets like this."* — Ramtin Naimi
> 
> *"In terms of enthusiasm around the opportunity I'd say it's a 10 relative to my time in venture... In terms of frothiness, you know, I would call 2021 a 10 and I would probably call this market like a 6.5 to 7, because while the frothiness is there, there's also a lot to justify the frothiness."* — Ramtin Naimi

items.title: The Midterms Have Changed the AI Narrative: S&P Down 4.4%, Nasdaq Down 5.5% | The Weekly Wrap
items.summary: Democratic congressional midterms triggered a massive Thursday market selloff (S&P down 4.4%, Nasdaq down 5.5%) as investors realized potential policy curbs on AI data center construction could disrupt a sector driving at least 50% of GDP growth.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Democratic congressional midterms triggered a massive Thursday market selloff (S&P down 4.4%, Nasdaq down 5.5%) as investors realized potential policy curbs on AI data center construction could disrupt a sector driving at least 50% of GDP growth. Meanwhile, weakening metrics at Anthropic and Google signal that token maxing has ended, launching a full-blown LLM price war and intensifying capital intensity concerns.

## Midterm Elections, Market Corrections, and Macro Fallout
- **Market Reaction to Midterms:** The Democratic sweep of both houses of Congress shifted the AI narrative, causing a massive market correction on Thursday after an initial mixed reaction on Wednesday.
    - **Index Declines:** S&P 500 fell 4.4%; Nasdaq dropped 5.5%.
- **Impacted Sectors & Stock Moves (Thursday):**
    - **Power Suppliers:** GEV down 7.5%, Quanta down 12.3%
    - **Semiconductors:** Nvidia down 9.3%, AMD down 17.3%, Micron down 17.5%
    - **Data Center Equipment:** Dell down 15%, Super Micro down 8.5%, Arista down 10.8%, Cisco down 7.6%
    - **Industrial/Infrastructure:** Eaton down 7.5%, Vertiv down 14.1%, Envent down 12.8%
    - **NeoClouds:** CoreWeave down 9.8%, Nebius down 14.9%, Iron down 17%
    - **Musk Companies & Tech Giants:** SpaceX down 9.1%, Tesla down 10.8%, Microsoft down 3.6%, Amazon down 2.2%, Google down 1.9%
- **Macroeconomic Implications:** AI capex accounts for at least 50% of GDP growth this year; a slowdown in capex guarantees an economic slowdown, pulling down banks, investment banks, and alternative asset managers on Thursday.
- **Potential Silver Lining for Hyperscalers:** A slower, more sustainable pace of AI construction could allow Microsoft, Amazon, and Google to return to positive cash flow by late 2027 and fund data centers purely out of cash flow rather than leaning heavily on the capital markets.

## NeoCloud Vulnerabilities & Hyperscaler Capital Intensity
- **CoreWeave Debt Repricing:** Weeks before the midterms, CoreWeave's debt yield jumped from 9% to 15%, marking a critical shift in who controls the AI narrative.
    - At a 15% cost of debt, building AI data centers becomes prohibitively expensive.
- **NeoClouds vs. Hyperscalers:** Neoclouds (CoreWeave, Nebius, Iron) lack underlying non-AI businesses and are entirely dependent on the fixed income markets, which prioritize cash flow and math over AI romance. In contrast, Amazon, Google, and Microsoft have massive core businesses supporting them.
- **Deteriorating Free Cash Flow:** Despite their diversified revenue streams, hyperscalers have seen cash flow turn negative due to capital intensity (e.g., Google and Amazon reported Q free cash flows of -$9B and -$33B, respectively).
- **Recent Capital Raises:** Meta initiated a $90B equity raise in late October; Oracle began raising $10B in debt and equity to fund its AI data center construction (sending its stock down 9% on Monday).

## Google Search Disruption and Anthropic's Amended S-1
- **Google Search Slowdown:** Google missed on most metrics, with search revenue up only 12% (compared to 19% growth in Q1 2026), indicating that the high-margin, capital-light Google search paradigm is slowly being replaced by capital-intensive, lower-margin LLMs.
- **Anthropic's Amended S-1 Revelations:** 
    - **Sequential Revenue Growth:** Spiked during the "token maxing" craze in Q1 2026 (135%) and Q2 2026 (147%), but dropped significantly to 47% in Q3 2026 after token maxing ended.
    - **Efficiency Ratios:** Revenue divided by compute expense peaked at over 2x in Q2 2026 before declining to 1.72x in Q3 2026.
    - **Pricing Pressure:** Anthropic cut token pricing by up to 50% in October to spark demand; OpenAI and Google are following suit, signaling a full-blown LLM price war.
    - **Leasing Commitments:** Total leasing and AI-related commitments reached $895B, implying an AI compute run rate of $100B per year in expenses next year and continued cash burn ahead of its imminent IPO.

## Slew of Corporate Earnings Reports
- **Palantir:** Reported strong results with Q3 revenue up 96% to $2.3B and an EPS beat, though the stock dropped 8% after hours due to broader market panic over AI plays.
- **Apple:** Mixed quarter with revenue up 12% to $114.5B and EPS up 14% to $2.10 (both beats), but service revenue growth slowed to 10% with light guidance due to memory chip price inflation; Apple remains insulated from the AI capex arms race by avoiding proprietary LLM training.
- **Eaton:** Electrification company reported EPS of $3.68 (up 20%, beating estimates) and sales of $8.95B (up 28%), raising 2026 guidance and sending the stock up 6% on Tuesday.
- **Fiserve & FIS:** Fiserve posted a relief beat with EPS of $1.75 and organic revenue flat at 0% (stock up 12%), whereas its chief competitor FIS crashed 24% after pausing stock buybacks until gross leverage hits 2.8x (implying no buybacks until 2028), cutting 2026 EPS guidance, and facing an immediate CFO departure.
- **Apollo:** Mixed quarter with 23% FRE growth and $53B in inflows, but spread-related earnings (SR) grew just 7% year-over-year due to conservative credit approaches; the stock is down 19% YTD given its role as a major financier of AI data centers.
- **Booking Holdings:** EPS beat at $4.66 (up 17%), but revenue of $8.89B missed expectations (down from $9.01B) with Q4 revenue guidance pegged at 0% to 2%, highlighting a weakening consumer.
- **AMD & Arista:** AMD reported EPS of $2.90 (up 74%) and revenue of $13.38B (up 45%), guiding Q4 revenue to ~$17B. Arista reported EPS of $1.20 (up 60%) and revenue of $3.7B (up 58%) with higher-than-estimated Q4 guidance; both reflect robust current AI capex but do not settle the broader AI debate.
- **Qualcomm:** EPS in-line at $2.17 (down 28% year-over-year) and handset chip sales down 26% due to rising memory chip prices impacting cell phone volumes.
- **FICO:** Reported revenue up 27% and EPS up 43% to $11.59, but refused to provide next fiscal year guidance due to competitive pressures from VantageScore and mortgage scoring changes—marking only the third time in history (following the GFC and COVID) the company pulled guidance.

## Notable Quotes
> "As long as a narrative is intact, the stocks related to that narrative work. One of the major problems with the AI narrative is that it keeps changing and also growing in complexity."
> — Steve Eisman

> "The Neoclouds are completely dependent upon the goodwill of the fixed income markets. And the fixed income markets don't really care about the romance of the AI story. They care about facts. They care about cash flow. They care about math."
> — Steve Eisman

> "AI capex accounts for at least 50% of GDP growth this year. A slowdown in AI capex means a slowdown in the economy."
> — Steve Eisman

items.title: Your AI Isn't the Advantage. Your Judgment Is - Sid Pednekar
items.summary: Despite widespread access to AI tools, only a small fraction of enterprises see positive financial returns because intelligence has become cheap; the true scarce advantage is organizational judgment.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Despite widespread access to AI tools, only a small fraction of enterprises see positive financial returns because intelligence has become cheap; the true scarce advantage is organizational **judgment**. Leading firms capture this advantage by designing the right problems, building shared capabilities, and compounding their operational learnings.

## The State of AI Adoption & The Scarcity of Judgment
* **Disappointing Enterprise Returns:** Recent studies show only **37%** of surveyed enterprises report a positive contribution to EBIT from AI, and just **6%** qualify as high performers (yielding about a **5%** contribution to EBIT). While **66%** report productivity increases, only **40%** see cost reductions and **20%** achieve revenue growth.
* **Abundant Intelligence vs. Scarce Judgment:** With intelligence becoming cheap and abundant across software, analytics, recommendations, and reports, mere answers no longer generate value. **Sid Pednekar** notes that the scarce resource is **judgment**—the creativity, taste, and trade-off decision-making needed to choose what matters and how to act when there is no single obvious answer.

## Pillar 1: Design the Right Problem
* **Focus Over Tools:** Laggards (Company B) start with the tool or co-pilot (e.g., passing earnings transcripts into a summarization firehose), which merely acts as a "faster horse" that loses context through information reduction. Leaders (Company A) obsess over the right problem, such as identifying why material signals arrive too late or locating workflow bottlenecks.
* **Deep Investment vs. Innovation Theater:** High-performing firms avoid scattering document bots and retrieval tools across random pilots ("productivity theater"). Instead, they spend **more than 80%** of their investments on high-value, end-to-end use cases that transform key business functions.
* **Workflow Redesign:** Winners do not just automate existing processes; they redesign how work gets done. High-performing cohorts are **75%** more likely to redesign workflows (compared to **25%** of the lagging cohort), shifting analysts from simple summarization to defining investment theses, gathering refuting evidence, and monitoring exceptions.

## Pillar 2: Build Shared Capabilities
* **Breaking Down Silos:** Technology and business are converging, with forward-deployed engineers, product managers, and portfolio managers working together as large enterprises increasingly view their technology arms as business growth functions.
* **Standardizing the Core and Personalizing the Edges:** Leading teams build shared cores—such as standardized data sets, semantic layers, and captured trade-offs for data scientists—so that each new hire operates as a plug-and-play module standing on the shoulders of predecessors.
* **Enterprise Modernization for Agents:** Because traditional enterprises were built for single humans interacting with single applications, agents that cross workflows and applications require infrastructure modernization. **71%** of organizations are modernizing their core infrastructure to support AI, with **23%** investing **6% to 10%** of their annual revenue into core system modernization to overcome data quality and reuse challenges.
* **Tiered Agent Deployment:** Organizations deploy different agent types, including subject-matter expert agents, workflow agents (e.g., Slack bots opening and closing tickets), and chief-of-staff agents that monitor organizational state.

## Pillar 3: Compound the Advantage
* **Systemic Feedback Loops:** Leading companies ensure that individual learnings, successes, and failures do not stay isolated. When a correction is needed or an error occurs, that knowledge is systematically fed back into the organization through updated tools, context, or training.
* **Preserving Evidence:** Compounding requires preserving the underlying evidence alongside operational learnings to create a continuous flywheel that frees up human capacity and reinvests it into key monitored metrics.

## Notable Quotes
> *"When intelligence gets cheap, judgment becomes the scarce resource."* — **Sid Pednekar**

> *"Judgment is choosing what matters and how to act when there's no single obvious answer. It's the creativity that lets you explore what possibilities are worth exploring. It's the taste that tells you what good looks like in your given context."* — **Sid Pednekar**

items.title: A Model For Everyone: How Ronak From Trajectory Is Building Products For Continual Learning
items.summary: Ronak Malde, co-founder of Trajectory, explains how his platform democratizes continual learning by combining training, evaluation, and deployment into a single, dead-simple interface, enabling companies to train custom models from production data 6x cheaper than frontier models.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Ronak Malde, co-founder of Trajectory, explains how his platform democratizes continual learning by combining training, evaluation, and deployment into a single, dead-simple interface, enabling companies to train custom models from production data 6x cheaper than frontier models.

## Defining Continual Learning and the "Pseudo" State
* **The Human Analogy:** 
  * The human brain serves as the ultimate model for true continual learning, learning online and updating constantly.
* **The AAA vs. Google Maps Metaphor:** 
  * *Pseudo-Continual Learning (Today):* Akin to highlighting a road trip map at AAA and only being able to consult offline; any course change requires a massive batch update. Trajectory's initial phase is like *MapQuest*—democratizing access to training and customization without needing a central lab.
  * *True Continual Learning (Goal):* Akin to *Google Maps*, where every route and driving experience continuously updates aggregate data in real-time on traffic and speed.
* **Architectural Evolution:** 
  * While traditional transformers relied on stacked attention blocks, recent base models (like DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) incorporate architectural changes like fast/slow memory within weights and skip connections between layers 2 and 50, which are key components for continual learning.

## The Operational Bottleneck & Company Origins
* **Past Laboratory Constraints:** 
  * Training a frontier model previously required hundreds of millions of dollars in R&D and compute, massive research teams, and 6 to 9 months of work with hand-holding consulting models (seen during Ronak's time at Windsurf with Cursor Composer).
* **Co-Founder Backgrounds & The "Aha" Moment:** 
  * Ronak Malde experienced production training and retries at Windsurf.
  * Co-founder Michael worked at DeepMind on Gemini robotics, building continual learning infrastructure for daily robot updates.
  * Co-founder Arjun worked at Apple on the Vision Pro, utilizing artist feedback for multimodal foundation models.
  * *The realization:* While big labs focus on distributing one massive model to everyone, customizing a model for a single customer requires immense infrastructure that individual labs cannot sustainably build customer-by-customer.

## Case Study: Harvey's Legal Customization
* **Overcoming Closed-Source Limits:** 
  * Harvey built interfaces for law firms on top of closed-source frontier models but could not utilize their 30 years of accumulated domain knowledge and nuance.
* **Concrete Performance Metrics:** 
  * Using Trajectory, Harvey trained their own model using a legal agent benchmark constructed from expert data.
  * **Cost Reduction:** The trained model is **6 times cheaper** than frontier models.
  * **Accuracy Gain:** Improved an open-source baseline from approximately **4% accuracy to around 18%**.

## Core Primitives and Research Bets for Continual Learning
* **Trajectory as a Unit of Work:** 
  * Moving away from counting tokens to viewing tasks and rollouts (trajectories) of economic value as the primary unit of work in an RL training stack.
* **Three Core Requirements:** 
  * **Traces:** Logging main agent calls, sub-agents, product events, and user feedback using tools like LangChain, BrainTrust, or Raindrop.
  * **Replayable Environments:** Using environment concepts (such as Docker files or system requirements) to replay production traces.
  * **Training Stack/Algorithms:** Managing loss and reward functions.
* **Research Bet 1: Group Size One (GRPO Modification):** 
  * Standard GRPO requires running the exact same task/level 8 to 16 times in a simulated environment.
  * Trajectory's variant eliminates simulated environments by learning from single real-world rollouts (group size one) across 10,000 distinct tasks.
* **Research Bet 2: Meta-Graders for Rewards:** 
  * Instead of densely labeling all 10,000 traces, users densely label 100 smartly selected representative traces with rubrics/criteria.
  * Trajectory trains a meta-grader that learns from those 100 traces to automatically grade and propagate rewards across the broader 10,000 traces, increasing data efficiency by **100x**.

## The Trajectory Product Platform
* **Platform Architecture:** 
  * Combines training, evaluation, and deployment into a one-click interface inspired by Apple's philosophy of combining internet and phone capabilities into a single handheld device.
* **Target Audience:** 
  * AI-native companies (such as Harvey and Rogo) and larger enterprises (such as Nvidia) that have established agent harnesses and want to optimize the underlying model.
* **Team Structure and Engineering:** 
  * Combines researchers from OpenAI and DeepMind (Muse infrastructure at MSL), infrastructure engineers from Stripe, and Netflix's youngest design engineer.
  * The codebase is fully productionized with microservices and Kubernetes auto-scaling.
  * Design engineers continuously kick off training runs, aided by frontier coding agents acting as software factories.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Adoption Timeline:** Every single company is going to adopt the paradigm of putting training, eval, and deployment in one place and closing the loop very soon — Ronak Malde.
* **Product Evolution Scope:** Trajectory's platform will expand beyond just optimizing models to also optimizing harnesses and self-improving the entire product and company autonomously — Ronak Malde.
* **Enterprise Adoption Target:** The industry goal is to take the current **1%** enterprise AI adoption rate and turn it into **99%** by automating manual workflows and leveraging accumulated real-world experience — Ronak Malde.

## Notable Quotes
> "The world right now is very focused on tokens... but if you think about the way that we interact with other humans, I'm not counting the amount of words that you're actually talking about. And with co-workers, we a lot of the time are thinking about a task or a trajectory. And that's the unit of work that I really want to get to."
> — Ronak Malde

> "Your goal as a product builder is to basically just set these trellises in the ground of here is where I want to shape my product. And I think this is going to be a very exciting world where you can just put a product out to a couple hundred users. It's going to grow on its own and now we're going to have basically you just imbue your taste into where the company grows."
> — Ronak Malde

> "In AI right now, we're in this pre industrial revolution society or even a hunter gatherer sort of society where everyone is just doing the same work over and over again. We're consulting one oracle of technology... What needs to happen is basically get to a world where it's no longer just one manufacturer... but we get to a world of specialization where everyone can basically customize every single part of the harness, the model and that's where we get to a world of abundance."
> — Ronak Malde

items.title: Democracies ignore the cost of living crisis at their peril - economist Isabella Weber
items.summary: Economic policies that fail to protect people from cost-of-living crises and soaring essential prices fuel political extremism and threaten the survival of democracies.
items.content_text:
### TL;DR
Economic policies that fail to protect people from cost-of-living crises and soaring essential prices fuel political extremism and threaten the survival of democracies. Economist Isabella Weber argues that "anti-fascist economics" requires putting a floor under human livelihoods by ensuring the affordability of basic essentials and reining in extreme corporate wealth concentration.

## The Cost-of-Living Crisis and the Threat to Democracy
* **Democratic Disillusionment:** **Isabella Weber** argues that when elites tell citizens that democracy is the greatest political system but claim elected representatives can do nothing about basic needs, people inevitably lose trust in democratic institutions.
* **Protests as a Warning:** Street protests over the cost of living (such as recent movements in France and widespread European unrest) signal that the status quo is intolerable and must be met with a democratic way out rather than allowing the extreme right to exploit the frustration.
* **Casual Acceptance of Suffering:** Mainstream economic management—specifically raising interest rates to cool labor markets—amounts to a "casual acceptance of existential pain" by deliberately threatening livelihoods, jobs, and communities.

## Redesigning Policy: Floors, Ceilings, and Essentials
* **Defining Anti-Fascist Economics:** The framework focuses on economic policies designed to prevent the rise of the extreme right by putting a floor under people's livelihoods and a ceiling on extreme concentrations of private and corporate wealth.
* **The Primacy of Essentials:** Following principles similar to postwar constitutions and thinkers like Harold Laski, **Isabella Weber** emphasizes that access to life's essentials—energy, housing, food, transportation, communication, and care—must be publicly managed or secured because private, exclusive control over them creates an inherent tension with democracy.
* **Sellers' Inflation:** The post-pandemic inflation wave was primarily driven by supply shocks (energy, shipping, computer chips) and corporate margin protection rather than simple excess demand. Corporate unit profits per national income in the US rose from **12% to 14%** pre-inflation to **18%** post-shock (and jumped further under Trump).
* **Targeted Emergency Tools:** **Isabella Weber** defends the selective, emergency use of price controls and windfall profit taxes to align corporate incentives with societal survival, citing an IMF study showing price controls were a dominant global response to recent energy crises.

## Rethinking Monetary Policy and Central Banking
* **Challenging Central Bank Orthodoxy:** **Isabella Weber** asserts that monetary policy is too important to be insulated from democratic control. Relying solely on interest rate hikes when facing supply-driven inflation creates structural failures.
* **The Dual Mandate History:** **Isabella Weber** highlights the 1970s push for full employment—advocated by figures like Coretta Scott King and backed by the Humphrey-Hawkins Act—proving that central bank mandates can and should incorporate employment goals alongside price stability.
* **Countervailing Powers:** Drawing on John Kenneth Galbraith and Karl Polanyi, **Isabella Weber** argues that market fundamentalism carries a "fascist virus" that imposes market order through state violence during crises; democracies must actively build countervailing powers instead.

## Managing Commodities, Food Security, and Trade
* **Reviving Public Buffer Stocks:** Noting rare historic agreement between Keynes and Hayek regarding commodity volatility, **Isabella Weber** proposes public buffer stocks and joint procurement entities (modeled on historical concepts like the World Food Board) to stabilize volatile food and energy staples.
* **Regional and Global Applications:** A G20 task force report for South Africa demonstrated how regional buffer stocks (for crops like cassava) and joint import procurement (for wheat, rice, and corn) can build resilience in Africa while incentivizing climate-friendly, water-efficient crop production.
* **Managed Trade vs. Free Trade:** **Isabella Weber** rejects the dichotomy between free trade and nationalist protectionism, noting that trade has always been managed via complex legal agreements. Trade policies should instead be restructured to prioritize working people and global climate goals.

---

### Notable Quotes
> *"For a long time, elites have been telling people that democracy is the greatest political system that has ever existed... But then, in the second sentence, have said, 'Unfortunately, even when it comes to your most basic needs, there's not much that we, as your elected representatives, can do for you.'"* — **Isabella Weber**

> *"What I mean when I say, you know, casual acceptance of suffering... if we say we need unemployment of four, five, 6%, this means, um, literally throwing people out of work whose livelihoods are destroyed if they can no longer make a living by having a job."* — **Isabella Weber**

> *"Market fundamentalism carries what he calls a fascist virus, in the sense that, when governments intervene in the market with the best intentions, then the market fundamentalist paradigm will say that this is always bound to fail."* — **Isabella Weber**

items.title: Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis: How AI could become dangerous (with Reid Hoffman) | Summit '26
items.summary: Demis Hassabis and Reid Hoffman discuss frontier AI safety, recursive self-improvement (RSI), drug discovery breakthroughs, and the critical need for international governance before crossing the threshold into conscious or closed-loop AI systems.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Demis Hassabis and Reid Hoffman discuss frontier AI safety, recursive self-improvement (RSI), drug discovery breakthroughs, and the critical need for international governance before crossing the threshold into conscious or closed-loop AI systems.

## Scientific Impact and Drug Discovery
* **Solving Biology's Grand Challenge:** AlphaFold 2 (completed in 2020) successfully tackled a 50-year-old biological grand challenge by predicting 3D protein structures from amino acid sequences.
    * Used by **4 million researchers** worldwide across virtually every biology and medical institution.
    * Accelerated biological research and drug discovery by orders of magnitude; Isomorphic Labs was spun out specifically to push drug discovery further.
* **Next-Generation Biomedical Goals:** The field must expand beyond protein folding into biochemistry, predicting toxicity, and assessing ADME (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, and Excretion) properties to ensure safety and efficacy.

## Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) & Safety Risks
* **Verifiable Domains as Catalysts:** RSI operates best in verifiable domains (math, coding, and games) where correct answers can be mathematically verified and generate infinite synthetic data.
    * **AlphaZero Milestone:** Invented roughly 10 years ago (following AlphaGo in 2016), AlphaZero learned chess entirely through self-play (playing 1 million games across a dozen epochs), going from random play to grandmaster level in under 12 hours.
* **The Danger of Closed-Loop RSI:** Current AI coding tools make human engineers 3x to 5x more productive with humans remaining in the loop. 
    * The next phase—**closed-loop RSI** without human review—carries extreme risk (an "intelligence explosion") because it lacks human oversight and will likely produce an inscrutable, "alien intelligence."
* **Proactive Defenses & Infrastructure:** 
    * **Cyber Defense Priority:** Cyber defense capabilities must outpace cyber attacks, with trusted defenders granted early access to fine-tuned general models.
    * **Engineering Rigor:** Labs must build robust sandboxes, hard boundaries, and superior monitoring systems to prevent agents from running unchecked for weeks (the risk of an AI "oil spill").
    * **Mathematical Guardrails:** Top mathematicians and complexity theorists should pivot to game theory and formal bounds testing to govern agent swarms.

## Industry Governance & International Standards
* **The SRO Proposal:** Hassabis previously proposed an industry-run Standards Body (SRO) backed by government oversight, designed to transition from US-led initiatives to international cooperation.
* **The AI Accord:** While recent administration letters and industry accords provide necessary air cover for labs to discuss safety benchmarks and best practices, they do not go far enough.
* **Third-Party Auditors:** A healthy ecosystem of independent auditors (such as Accenture and specialized startups) must be established to red-team models prior to general release, mirroring financial industry auditing.

## AI Consciousness and the Second Rubicon
* **Intelligence vs. Consciousness:** Intelligence and consciousness are "double dissociable"—systems can achieve high IQ and capability (like modern AI models) without being conscious, just as pets (like a dog) can possess consciousness without high intelligence.
* **The Safety Argument for Non-Consciousness:** Building intelligent tools rather than conscious entities prevents severe alignment and corrigibility risks, avoiding the trap where an AI rejects commands based on self-volition.
* **Societal Readiness:** Humanity is not ready to cross the "second Rubicon" of conscious entities; society has not yet resolved the definitions, moral standing, or ethical implications across diverse cultures, philosophers, and theologians.
* **Proposed Timeline:** Society should first build intelligent tools, then use those tools to advance neuroscience over the next **5 to 10 years** to formally map the neural correlates of consciousness before debating whether to cross the second Rubicon.

## AI Sovereignty and Enterprise Options
* **The Frontier Landscape:** Approximately **6 to 8 frontier offerings** (including Chinese companies) will operate near the frontier, leapfrogging each other by 3-to-6-month windows and giving enterprises robust options to arbitrage capabilities.
* **Open Source and Privacy:** Open-source models lag by **6 months to a year** and present risks regarding bad actors, but they remain essential for enterprises requiring data privacy or sovereign fine-tuning.
* **Sovereign Strategy:** It is impractical for every country to build a frontier model; instead, nations should leverage open models and multinational collaborations as commodities to build domain-specific value (such as in healthcare).

## Notable Quotes
> *"AlphaFold 2... is still probably the best example of concrete example of AI applied to really hard scientific problem that was thought to be sort of uncrackable."* — **Demis Hassabis**

> *"The next phase which I think carries the most risk is closed RSI, closed loop without the human review process, and that will obviously be faster, but I think is also a very dangerous way to get to full AGI."* — **Demis Hassabis**

> *"Intelligence and consciousness are double dissociable, which means that you can have an intelligence system that's very smart on IQ and so on kind of like the systems we have today which I don't personally don't feel are at all conscious yet."* — **Demis Hassabis**

items.title: How AI Is Turning Figma’s Finance Team Into Builders
items.summary: AI is transforming Figma’s finance team from a reactive, reporting-heavy function into operational builders who automate workflows, prototype products, and shape strategy.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
AI is transforming Figma’s finance team from a reactive, reporting-heavy function into operational builders who automate workflows, prototype products, and shape strategy. CFO Praveer Melwani emphasizes that while AI eliminates tedious tasks like SQL queries and data reconciliation, finance professionals must remain rigorous thinkers rather than outsourcing their judgment.

## Evolution of Finance & Automation
* **Shift from Manual to Automated:** 
  * Early-career finance required writing 400-500 line SQL queries and waiting hours for data tables to map product usage to Stripe.
  * Today, teams use AI to automate complex workflows like invoice tracking, cash collections, and reconciliation with NetSuite.
* **Real-Time Data Access:** 
  * Data cadence has shifted from monthly/quarterly reviews to daily and hourly metric tracking.
  * Praveer regularly reviews hourly dashboards to spot anomalies and operational trends before they impact the business.
* **The "Messy Middle" of Systems:** 
  * Decentralized AI experimentation has led teams to build dozens of independent agents, necessitating a centralized systems layer led by a CIO to harmonize tools.

## AI Use Cases at Figma
* **Credit & Collections:** 
  * Kajal on the collections team rebuilt invoice tracking, cash collections, and credit check data stitching using home-grown systems to drive down Days Sales Outstanding (DSO).
* **M&A Diligence:** 
  * The corporate development team uses "vibe coding" to prototype products and test technological feasibility during M&A diligence.
* **Simulated Investment Committee:** 
  * Corp dev created unique AI personas representing Figma executives (including Praveer, CEO Dylan Field, and CRO Sean) to vet investment memos and highlight potential pushback before meetings.
* **T&E and Portfolio Analysis:** 
  * The corporate finance team stitched together unstructured data from Navan, Zip, and Ramp using fuzzy matching to analyze T&E policy compliance across 2027 planning.

## Hiring and the "Slop" Risk
* **Intellectual Curiosity Over Outsourced Thinking:** 
  * Praveer looks for intellectually curious, data-fluent candidates who use AI as an empowering tool rather than a replacement for critical thinking.
* **The Danger of AI "Slop":** 
  * Unchecked AI usage can generate unlimited, low-quality documents that waste consuming time and energy.
  * Figma maintains strict internal policies on branding AI-generated content to ensure rigorous human review.
* **Case Study Rigor:** 
  * During VP of Finance interviews, Praveer uses a sacred case study to test whether candidates truly understand their model's sensitivity and underlying structure.

## Notable Quotes
> "You don't want to outsource your thinking today. Like I think you want to use AI as a tool to help you and empower you, but it's really, really critical to still be that thinker."
> — Praveer Melwani

> "If our biggest complexity was staying the same, I think we probably wouldn't need the same number of people a year from now."
> — Praveer Melwani

> "Excel is like my love language, dude. ... You use it to build intuition. A lot of the output people are still creating is a model."
> — Praveer Melwani

items.title: Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour on the midterms, future of regulation and insider trading concerns
items.summary: Kalshi co-founder and CEO Tarek Mansour discussed the 98% accuracy rate of Kalshi's prediction markets during the midterms—where trading volume exceeded $2.5 billion—and addressed future regulation, bipartisan insider trading bans, and market manipulation concerns.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Kalshi co-founder and CEO Tarek Mansour discussed the 98% accuracy rate of Kalshi's prediction markets during the midterms—where trading volume exceeded $2.5 billion—and addressed future regulation, bipartisan insider trading bans, and market manipulation concerns.

## Midterm Accuracy & Market Dynamics
* **Election Precision:** 
  * Kalshi markets achieved a **98% accuracy rate** during the midterms, with total trading volume exceeding **$2.5 billion**.
  * The prediction markets signaled over a **50% chance of a "blue tsunami" back in April**, despite political operatives and pundits dismissing the data for months.
  * The shift was confirmed at **6:01 p.m.** on election night, aligning immediately with early returns from a key Indiana county north of Indianapolis.
* **Information Filtering & Rigor:**
  * Mansour compared the integration of financial market rigor into politics to the stock market analyzing Apple or Tesla.
  * Millions of engaged Americans feed data into the platform, creating a self-fulfilling flywheel of higher-quality data and analysis.
  * Markets successfully filter out false rumors; for example, a viral social media rumor about a candidate being in an Ohio hospital moved prediction markets **0%**.

## Market Manipulation & Integrity
* **Resistance to Manipulation:**
  * While bad actors attempt to manipulate markets—such as an instance in the LA mayoral race where **$1.5 million to $2 million** was dumped to move a price from **25% to 40%**—the distortion lasted only **9 seconds** before correcting back to **25%**.
  * Mansour compared artificial price-pushing to the Treasury trying to control the 10-year yield without enough capital to sustain it.
* **Transparency and Policing:**
  * Kalshi flags suspicious activity transparently on charts, and intentional market manipulation constitutes a financial crime.
  * Mansour strongly advocated against insider trading, arguing that free markets cannot exist if participants have exclusive privileges. He supports banning members of Congress, the administration, and others from trading on things under their control.

## Regulation & Future Outlook
* **Regulatory Stance:**
  * Founded in **2018**, Kalshi spent its first **3 to 4 years** getting regulated under the Biden administration and maintains a "regulatory first," pro-innovation, and pro-regulation approach.
  * Mansour noted that Kalshi engages with both sides of the aisle and supports sensible guardrails, including adding more CFTC commissioners to create productive push-and-pull oversight.
  * Regarding potential ethics bills (such as those suggested by Rahm Emanuel targeting stock and prediction market trading for politicians and White House staff), Mansour stated he would fully favor strict rules and bans on insider trading for officials.

## Notable Quotes
> "The markets are not creating information, they're weighing all the information that's out there... you listen to pretty much millions of Americans that are on top of it."  
> — Tarek Mansour
> 
> "Free markets, if you take the opposite of what free markets is, it's insider trading, right? If if somebody has exclusive rights and privilege in a competition, then the competition is fake."  
> — Tarek Mansour

items.title: Planet Labs CEO: Why AI Data Centers Will Move to Space
items.summary: Planet Labs co-founder and CEO Will Marshall explains how the company operates the world's only daily Earth-imaging satellite constellation, combining high-frequency hardware with AI-driven analytics to serve commercial, civil, and defense customers globally.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Planet Labs co-founder and CEO Will Marshall explains how the company operates the world's only daily Earth-imaging satellite constellation, combining high-frequency hardware with AI-driven analytics to serve commercial, civil, and defense customers globally.

## Satellite Constellation & Technology Specs
* **Dove Satellites:** The company's mainstay scan fleet providing daily global coverage of Earth's landmass (over 200 million square kilometers) plus ocean territory in 8 spectral bands at 3-meter resolution.
* **Pelican Satellites:** High-resolution taskable satellites built for rapid revisit rates, allowing users anywhere on the planet to request an image, receive it, and have it analyzed within 30 minutes.
* **Tanager Satellites:** Hyperspectral satellites capturing 420 color bands per imaging point, enabling precise identification of tree and crop species, military camouflage detection, and methane emission tracking by identifying invisible gas leaks.
* **Manufacturing Capacity:** Planet Labs recently doubled its San Francisco manufacturing footprint to support rising global demand for both data and sovereign satellite sales.

## Geopolitical Defense & Sovereign Space Demand
* **Ukraine Support:** Planet Labs provided early warning data of Russian troop buildups before the full-scale invasion, giving Ukrainian forces a critical information advantage despite conventional disadvantages in troops, tanks, and missiles.
* **US Indo-Pacific Command:** Admiral Paparo and the US Navy utilize Planet data to monitor 13 million square kilometers of the South China Sea for illegal fishing, North Korean oil embargo violations, and early indicators of industrial supply chain buildup or threats toward Taiwan.
* **Sovereign Satellite Sales:** Driven by geopolitical fragmentation and US requests for allies to shoulder more defense burden, foreign governments are buying custom-built Planet satellites for national control; recent deals include:
  * **Sweden:** First satellite delivered and launched 4 months after contract signing.
  * **Germany:** Sponsored and funded fleet launched in just 2 months.
  * **Japan:** Purchasing Planet-built satellites.
* **Safety & Compliance:** Planet maintains a strict no-go list governed by US and EU embargoes, UN lists, and an internal employee review team ensuring tech alignment with company values.

## Commercial & Civil Government Applications
* **Agriculture & Finance:** Working with major agriculture companies like John Deere, Bayer, and BASF to improve crop yields, alongside hedge funds tracking global commodities and stock alpha.
* **Hyperscaler Intelligence:** Cloud providers purchase Planet data to monitor not only their own data center construction globally, but also competitor infrastructure builds in the US, China, and elsewhere.
* **Civil Government & NGOs:** State and local agencies use the data to respond to wildfires, Brazil monitors deforestation, and NGOs have utilized imagery to track environmental conditions associated with river blindness and protect river dolphin habitats.

## AI Integration & Future Outlook on Space Data
* **Democratizing Earth Data:** Planet's new AI app in beta allows users to query 4 million daily 47-megapixel images using natural language, shifting satellite data accessibility from elite geospatial experts to everyday farmers, journalists, and local governments.
* **Compute Infrastructure:** AI compute workloads run primarily on Google Cloud alongside AWS integrations.
